stories.title: 2 Bangladeshi men arrested for theft in Varanasi, passports seized:Came to India as tourists, turned to stealing after their belongings were stolen; sent to jail
stories.summary: Varanasi's Sarnath police have arrested two Bangladeshi nationals on charges of theft. They were caught with stolen goods at the Faridpur underpass. The arrested accused have been identified as Mohammed Bairul Islam and Mohammed Shafiqul Islam alias Munna. Both are residents of Chapai Nawabganj in Bangladesh. Police are now thoroughly verifying the authenticity of the Bangladeshi passports recovered from them. Stolen jewellery and mobile phones recovered Varuna Zone DCP Rajesh Pandey said, "Police teams were active to crack several theft cases in the police station area. As part of this effort, two youths were arrested while planning a theft. During questioning, it emerged that both were Bangladeshi nationals, and Bangladeshi passports were also recovered from them. Police questioning revealed that the accused had broken into a house in Amanpuri Colony and committed the theft on 19 October. They had already sold some of the stolen jewellery." Chose the path of crime after running out of money During questioning by the DCP, the accused admitted that they had come to India on valid visas about three months ago for tourism. They travelled from Bangladesh to Kolkata on 25 September and then went to Varanasi. While staying in Varanasi, all of Mohammad Shafiqul Islam's belongings were stolen, leaving him without money or any means of returning. After failing to find employment, they began breaking locks and committing thefts at night. Security agencies put on alert According to DCP Varuna Zone Rajesh Pandey, the police and other security agencies are questioning both accused and examining their past records. Acting on the government's instructions, the police had earlier verified people living in the city under suspicious circumstances. Both accused were sent to jail after being produced before the court.

stories.title: Swatantra Dev and Dayashankar Singh to engineer defections from SP:BJP forms joining committee; both have previously lured senior leaders away from the party
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party has entrusted Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh and Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh with the task of engineering defections from the Samajwadi Party and the Congress. The duo of Swatantra Dev and Dayashankar is considered successful in the politics of political manoeuvring. Before the 2022 Assembly elections, the duo had also brought more than 12 Samajwadi Party MLAs and Legislative Council members into the BJP. This time, too, the two have been assigned the responsibility of engineering defections involving several prominent Samajwadi Party leaders. The Samajwadi Party has launched a campaign to engineer defections in the BJP. Over the past 15 days, former BJP MP Dharmendra Kashyap, former Bisauli MLA Kushagra Sagar, former Dataganj MLA Sinod Kumar Shakya, BJP leader Akhilesh Pathak and Gonda district panchayat member Bhawani Bhim Shukla, along with their family members, have joined the BJP. Before the Assembly elections, the BJP has formed a joining committee to engineer defections in the Samajwadi Party, Congress and BSP. Livestock Minister and Rajya Sabha member Dharampal Singh has been appointed as the committee's chairperson. Former state president and Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi, former state president and former Union Minister Mahendranath Pandey, former state president and Water Resources Minister Swatantra Dev Singh, and Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh have been included in the committee. According to information, veteran BJP leader from Rohilkhand Dharmendra Kashyap has joined the Samajwadi Party. After this, former MLA Sinod Shakya also left the BJP and joined the Samajwadi Party. It is believed that, under Dharmendra Kashyap's influence, several prominent figures from the Shakya, Saini, Kushwaha and Kashyap communities may also join the Samajwadi Party. That is why charge of the joining committee has been given to Dharampal Singh, the BJP's prominent OBC leader in Rohilkhand. Meanwhile, according to BJP sources, the greatest anger and discontent within the party is in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand. In Purvanchal, the Samajwadi Party is trying to poach several BJP leaders. SP president Akhilesh Yadav himself is speaking to leaders who are angry with the BJP or whose induction into the SP would provide an electoral advantage. To prevent defections from the BJP in Purvanchal, the party has roped in prominent regional leaders Surya Pratap Shahi, Mahendranath Pandey and Dayashankar Singh. Swatantra Dev has been given responsibility for Bundelkhand. Swatantra and Dayashankar are adept at poaching Before the 2022 Assembly elections, the then Uttar Pradesh BJP president, Swatantra Dev Singh, assigned the party's then state vice-president, Dayashankar Singh, the responsibility of engineering defections from the Samajwadi Party. Dayashankar Singh brought SP MLCs Ravishankar Singh Pappu, Rama Niranjan and C.P. Chand, along with Narendra Bhati and around 12 MLAs and MLCs, into the BJP. He also facilitated Rakesh Sachan's defection from the Congress to the BJP. Before the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections, Dayashankar also played a major role in preparing seven SP MLAs to rebel. Strategy to break the Kurmi leadership The BJP has handed over the reins of the state presidency to Pankaj Chaudhary of the Kurmi community. The Yogi government also has prominent Kurmi leaders such as Swatantra Dev Singh and Ashish Patel serving as Cabinet ministers. However, the Kurmi community does not have a universally accepted leader in the state. Region-wise, the Samajwadi Party's Kurmi leaders are more influential than those of the BJP. In Awadh, they include Lalji Verma; in Bundelkhand, Naresh Uttam Patel and Krishna Devi Patel; in Purvanchal, SP Singh Patel, Ram Prasad Chaudhary and Ram Shiromani Verma; and in the Terai, Utkarsh Verma. The BJP wants to win over the Samajwadi Party's Kurmi leaders to prevent inroads into the Kurmi vote.

stories.title: Awadh Bar Association elections at Allahabad HC’s Lucknow Bench:5,000 lawyers to vote; association ID card mandatory for voting
stories.summary: Voting for the annual election of the Awadh Bar Association of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court will be held on Wednesday. Around five thousand lawyers will exercise their franchise. Voter slips have already been distributed to the electorate. Advocates must bring their COP certificates Advocates must bring either their COP certificate or Awadh Bar Association identity card to vote. Counting will begin on Thursday after polling and will continue until the results are declared. According to assistant election officer RBS Rathore, 11 candidates are contesting the post of president, while eight candidates are contesting the post of general secretary. The post of senior vice-president is reserved for women, with three women candidates contesting it. Meanwhile, 14 candidates are in the fray for the post of vice-president (middle) and 12 for vice-president (junior). The contest for the posts of joint secretary is also interesting. Along with male candidates, seven women candidates are contesting one seat reserved for women. 24 male candidates for four junior executive committee posts The treasurer's post is reserved for women, with 13 female candidates contesting it. Several candidates are also contesting executive committee posts. Twenty-five male candidates are contesting the four senior executive committee posts, while seven candidates are in the fray for the two posts reserved for women. Similarly, 24 male candidates are contesting the four junior executive committee posts, while seven female candidates are in the fray for the two posts reserved for women.

stories.title: Heavy rain alert in UP over next 24 hours:Cyclone Arnab to change weather, officials on alert; paddy crops may be affected
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh is set to change over the next 24 hours due to Cyclone Arnab. According to the Meteorological Department, heavy rain may occur in Purvanchal and Awadh from tomorrow, 29 to 31 October. Storms with winds reaching speeds of 140, accompanied by thunder and lightning, are likely. Meanwhile, Relief Commissioner Bhanu Chandra Goswami has directed officials in all districts of the state and relief control rooms to remain on alert for 24 hours. The police, health, irrigation and revenue department officials have been asked to stay vigilant, while district disaster control rooms have been directed to remain operational. The administration has been instructed to keep the necessary preparations in place to prevent loss of life and property due to storms and rain. Read now IMD and Agriculture Department issue guidelines for farmers Immediate harvesting and safe storage of crops: If your paddy or maize crop is 80 to 85% ripe, harvest it before 28 October. Do not leave the harvested crop in open fields or threshing grounds. Keep it under a permanent shed or at an elevated location and cover it properly with a strong tarpaulin. Arrangements to drain water from fields: Do not allow water to accumulate in vegetable, horticultural or paddy fields. For this, prepare drains at the corners of the fields in advance. Do not apply any fertiliser or spray pesticides in the fields for the next 3-4 days, and do not irrigate them. Insurance: If crops are damaged by stormy rain, farmers insured under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana must register their complaint on the toll-free number 14447 within 72 hours, so that compensation can be provided on time. Now know what damage Storm Arnab could cause in Uttar Pradesh Storm Arnab is likely to cause the most damage to crops. It is the final week of October. The paddy crop has ripened and is being harvested at this time. Preparations are also under way for sowing wheat, potatoes and mustard. In such circumstances, unseasonal rain and strong winds could undo the farmers' hard work. Rice to suffer the most damage: Prof. Ravi Shankar Singh, nodal officer at BHU's Rural Agriculture Weather Service Centre, and technical officer and meteorologist Shiv Mangal Singh said the rice crop is currently either fully ripened and ready for harvest or has been harvested and is lying in the fields. Strong winds (40-50 km/h) will flatten the rice plants in the fields. If the harvested rice is submerged in water, the grains will turn black and begin to rot. Vegetables and horticulture: Waterlogging in nurseries and fields of green vegetables such as cauliflower, tomatoes and chillies will cause the plants to rot. In addition, banana and papaya trees face the greatest risk of breaking or being uprooted because of the strong winds. Delay in sowing potatoes and mustard: Farmers who were planning to sow wheat, mustard or early potatoes at this time will be unable to sow for at least 10 to 15 days because of waterlogging in the fields. This could delay the entire rabi season. See in the graphics which city was the hottest and coldest in the past 24 hours

stories.title: Highway remains closed 36 hours after chemical tanker overturns:Traffic diverted against the flow in Lucknow; 20,000 residents report eye irritation
stories.summary: The highway remains closed 36 hours after a tanker loaded with formalin overturned on Kisan Path in the Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) area. Vehicles are being turned back, forcing everyone to return on the wrong side of the road. According to local residents, around 15,000 to 20,000 people have been affected. People are experiencing eye irritation and breathing difficulties. Several people complained of eye irritation, a feeling of nausea and breathing difficulties. Despite action by the police and relief and rescue teams after the accident, barricades remained in place on the highway even after 24 hours. Questions are also being raised over the lack of action against the factory operator. At around 6:30 p.m. on Monday, the tanker was carrying formalin from Sandila in Hardoi to a factory in the Gudamba area. The tanker became uncontrollable after a tyre burst near Manpur-Bana and overturned on the highway. This led to a chemical leak. After receiving information about the accident, BKT police reached the spot, barricaded the area around the site and stopped traffic. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force, State Disaster Response Force and fire service subsequently reached the spot. However, it took several hours to bring the chemical leak under control. Waited three hours for operation to stop leak to begin According to local residents, the police put up barricades around one kilometre from the site after the accident. The police, SDRF and fire service teams that reached the spot also remained at a distance from the tanker. It is alleged that for the first around three hours, the main action involved stopping people from going towards the site. Work to control the chemical leak began afterwards. It emerged that around eight truckloads of soil were dumped using several dumpers to control the leak. Despite this, people remained concerned about the chemical's impact in the area. Locally, it was said that the effects were felt up to around five kilometres away, while people within a radius of approximately two kilometres complained of irritation and other problems. Barricades remain in place 24 hours later; people leaving via the opposite direction On Tuesday, the day after the accident, barricades remained in place on the highway. As traffic was stopped, people had to take alternative routes. Some people were seen travelling in the wrong direction, creating a risk of road accidents. Local residents and passers-by faced difficulties as traffic remained affected for a long time. 20,000 people affected; questions raised over action Formalin leakage sparked panic and anger among people living in the surrounding area. Residents complained of eye irritation, a feeling of nausea and difficulty breathing. This has raised questions about who is responsible for the transportation of the hazardous chemical, safety arrangements and the action taken after the accident. Questions are also being raised over the lack of action against the factory operator after the accident. However, the official status of any action or investigation against the factory operator could not be independently confirmed. 30 minutes in a mock drill, several hours in reality... The tanker carrying formalin that overturned in Lucknow's BKT area has raised questions about disaster-management preparedness. NDRF and SDRF teams, which practise bringing situations under control within minutes during mock drills, spent several hours at the site trying to determine how to contain the chemical. This raises the question: if teams demonstrate their ability to bring situations under control quickly during mock drills, why did it take so long to contain the chemical during the actual incident? Was there a shortcoming in the preparations, or did the nature of the chemical make the challenge more difficult? The incident in BKT has highlighted the need to review the actual preparedness for disaster management, rapid response and the ability to deal with chemical disasters. Storage documents sought from factory owner ACP Bakshi Ka Talab Ankit Bansal said that the factory owner, Manu Gupta, had been asked to provide documents related to the storage of the chemical, while the tanker owner had been asked for transport-related documents. Six dumpers are being used to spread soil over the liquid that has spilled at the site. Police teams have been deployed to search for the accused driver. Driver had joined the job just three days earlier According to the ACP, questioning of the tanker's helper, Gaurav Mishra, a resident of Rampur in Hardoi, revealed that the driver, Manish, had joined duty just three days earlier. As a result, the factory owner did not have complete information about him. The police are gathering further information about the driver. Go to hospital if you experience eye irritation or difficulty breathing DG Health Pawan Kumar Arun, CMO Narendra Bahadur Singh and CHC superintendent J.P. Singh are present at the scene. The CHC superintendent said the chemical could spread rapidly through the air. Health camps have been set up some distance from the scene to help those affected. Two ambulances and a six-member medical team have been deployed. He said that anyone experiencing eye irritation or difficulty breathing should contact the hospital. If more people face problems, they can also go to the camp. People suffering from respiratory illnesses, asthma and tuberculosis need to take special precautions. Further action will be taken once the work is completed ACP Ankit Bansal said the chemical was being neutralised swiftly. The police have not yet been able to gather much information about the driver. Further action will be taken after the chemical removal work is completed. .

stories.title: FIR filed against attackers who used knives during idol immersion:Dispute broke out over dancing; injured man received 32 stitches
stories.summary: Gorakhpur police registered a case of attempted murder on Monday against 8-10 unidentified people for allegedly launching a deadly attack on a young man during an idol immersion. The incident took place near Aryanagar on the night of 21 October. Injured Akash Agrahari, 25, is undergoing treatment at BRD Medical College. He has received more than 32 stitches on his face, neck and hand. Police registered the case based on a complaint filed by Akash's cousin, Pradyumn. SP City Nimish Patil said surveillance and CCTV footage were being used to trace the accused. Police teams from Kotwali and Gorakhnath police stations are investigating the case. The accused will be arrested soon. Dispute broke out over dancing According to Aakash's cousin Pradyumn, who lives in Purana Gorakhpur, Gorakhnath, Aakash went to see the fair and take part in the idol immersion at around 10:45 p.m. on 21 October. He got into an argument with some youths leading the immersion procession over dancing. It is alleged that after one of the youths was removed from the spot, he returned with eight to 10 companions. They then attacked Aakash with knives and a bhujali. Aakash suffered serious injuries in the attack and collapsed on the road. Treatment under way at medical college Injured Akash was admitted to BRD Medical College. More than 32 stitches have been required on his face, neck and hand. He is undergoing treatment under doctors' supervision. The family has demanded an examination of footage from CCTV cameras installed around the scene of the incident. Akash's father, Vijay Agrahari, is frequently ill. The family says his difficulties have increased further after the attack on his son.

stories.title: 'Ganga Vilas' returns to Kashi with 30 foreign tourists:Visitors to stay for 3 nights and 2 days; visit Kashi Vishwanath temple and watch Ganga Aarti
stories.summary: The indigenous luxury river cruise 'Ganga Vilas', known for undertaking the world's longest river journey, has arrived in Kashi once again. The cruise, which departed from Kolkata, reached Varanasi via Ghazipur. It is carrying 30 tourists from several countries, including Germany and Switzerland. During their two-day, three-night stay in Kashi, the foreign guests will visit the Baba Vishwanath temple. They will also explore Sarnath's historical heritage and attend the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat. They will travel from the Vishwanath temple to Sarnath Preparations were made at the multi-modal terminal for the cruise's arrival. Arrangements are being made for the tourists' visit to Kashi. According to Raj Singh, chairman of the cruise operator Heritage River Journey (Antara), the tourists will visit Kashi's major religious and tourist sites. The 17 tourists travelling to Kolkata on the return journey will include 12 foreign nationals and five Indians. The Prime Minister had flagged it off in 2023 'Ganga Vilas' first arrived in Varanasi in January 2023. At the time, Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually flagged off the cruise from Ravidas Ghat in the presence of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Union Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal. The cruise then departed for Dibrugarh in Assam. Thirty-two foreign tourists were on board that journey. The cruise covered around 3,200 kilometres in 51 days. The route passes through the rivers of India and Bangladesh The 'Ganga Vilas' journey offers an opportunity to see historical sites, religious centres and natural landscapes along the rivers. Its designated route passes through the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, the India-Bangladesh Protocol Route and the Brahmaputra River. The journey includes several rivers, including the Ganga, Bhagirathi, Hooghly, Meghna, Padma, Jamuna and Brahmaputra. The cruise route passes through Bangladesh and the Indian states of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Assam. During the journey, tourists can closely experience the cultural diversity and historical heritage of India and Bangladesh, as well as the cities located along the riverbanks.

stories.title: SP wins Lucknow graduate seat by 17,000 votes:Akhilesh takes a dig at BJP, says it is ‘all out’ in MLC polls; results declared for 10 of 11 seats
stories.summary: The picture of the Legislative Council (MLC) elections in UP has become almost clear. Results for 10 out of 11 seats in the teacher and graduate quotas have been declared. The BJP has won 6 seats and the SP has won 4 seats. On the Lucknow Graduate seat, SP's Kanti Singh has secured victory by more than 17,000 votes. The BJP has received a double blow in Kashi. It suffered a defeat here on the Teacher seat, while its candidate is trailing on the Graduate seat. At 7:20 pm, counting had to be stopped for an hour. BJP candidate Kedarnath sat on a sit-in protest. He accused Observer Pranjal Yadav of orchestrating rigging. SP chief Akhilesh said, “Everyone understands the conspiracy to stop or slow down the counting of votes in Kashi, the BJP will not succeed in this. Counting has been resumed in Kashi. SP's Ashutosh Sinha is leading by over 9,000 votes.” In Gorakhpur, the BJP won by 307 votes in an extremely tight contest. Dhruv Tripathi has become an MLC for the fourth consecutive time. Independent candidate Rajiv Yadav, who gave him tough competition, said—'I have been deliberately defeated. A thousand votes have been stolen.' Upon Rajiv's defeat, his supporters burst into tears. On 23rd October, elections were held in 5 Graduate and 6 Teacher constituencies of the state. A total of 152 candidates were in the fray. Voting was conducted using ballot papers.

stories.title: 10 UP athletes compete at Para Asian Games:Swati wins Silver after paralysis; blind Simran bags Gold as husband guides her by holding her hand
stories.summary: India won 114 medals at the Para Asian Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Athletes from Uttar Pradesh contributed 13 of these medals, winning five gold, five silver and three bronze. These are not just medals, but the result of the struggles of 10 athletes who overcame difficult circumstances to achieve success. An athlete with visual impairment won gold by running the fastest. A woman whose legs were affected by polio won two medals for the country in a wheelchair. An athlete who spent six years confined to bed after an accident returned to win two medals in two different events. Read the inspiring stories of these athletes, their struggles and their success… Simran: Visually impaired athlete wins gold in 100m and 200m Simran was born prematurely at six and a half months at the home of Manoj Sharma in Modinagar, Ghaziabad. She spent six months in an incubator. After she recovered, her parents named her Simran. When she turned two, the family discovered that she could not see distant objects. Medical examinations revealed that her vision was limited to a distance of just six metres. Her family and neighbours were distressed, but her father refused to give up. He ensured that she received an education. When she joined Rukmani Modi Women's Inter College in Modinagar, she began focusing on athletics. At the 2021 Tokyo Paralympics, she finished 11th in the 100m T13 event but did not lose heart. She went on to win gold at the 2023 World Championships in Japan, two silver medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games and another gold at last year's World Para Athletics Championships. At the Aichi-Nagoya Games, Simran won gold in both the 100m and 200m events. Athletes in these races run with the assistance of guides. In Simran's case, her guide was her husband, Gajendra Singh, who is also an athlete in the Army. Since their marriage in 2017, Gajendra has continuously motivated her. Preeti Pal: Born with cerebral palsy, wins two silver medals Preeti was born in 2000 to Anil Pal in Hasampur village, Muzaffarnagar. Just six days after her birth, her leg began to bend abnormally. Doctors diagnosed her with cerebral palsy. She began walking with crutches and even underwent plaster treatment to straighten her leg. Later, her father left her in Meerut with her grandfather. Inspired by watching Paralympic athletes, Preeti began training at a stadium. She narrowly missed qualifying for the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics but went on to win gold at the National Para Games and the Khelo India Games. She finished fourth at the 2023 Asian Games before creating history by winning bronze at the 2024 Paralympics. She also won bronze at the World Para Athletics Championships the following year. Now, she has won two silver medals in the 100m and 200m events in Japan. Ayush Verma: Six years confined to bed, wins two medals in two events Ayush Verma from Meerut suffered an accident in 2014, sustaining a serious spinal cord injury that made it difficult for him to stand. He remained confined to bed for six years. In 2020, he began using a wheelchair and decided to pursue his goals from there. Ayush started training in both shot put and javelin throw. He delivered an outstanding performance at the Para Asian Games in Japan. First, he won gold in the F53 shot put with a throw of 8.16 metres. The very next day, he won bronze in the javelin throw. Ayush became the first Indian athlete to win medals in both events at the same tournament. Suvarna Raj: Polio affected both legs, but she wins gold Suvarna Raj was born in Nagpur, but her family now lives in Noida. Polio affected both her legs when she was just two years old. Walking became difficult, and she had to rely on a wheelchair. However, she refused to give up and pursued discus throw. She won bronze at the Fazza International Championships in Dubai, followed by gold and silver in Australia in early 2026. At the Asian Games in Japan, Suvarna won gold with her personal-best throw of 15.66 metres. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also congratulated her in a post on social media, saying, "You are the pride of Uttar Pradesh." Prachi Pandey: Software engineer wins bronze despite six surgeries Prachi Pandey from Unnao lives with spina bifida, a neurological condition. She cannot stand independently. After completing her MTech in Chandigarh, she became a software engineer, but her passion lay in sports. Initially, doctors advised her to stop playing, warning that her legs could weaken further and become paralysed. Prachi refused to give up and continued training at the Sports Authority of India's centre in Gandhinagar. She began competing in various para table tennis tournaments and won medals in countries including Germany, Brazil, Nigeria and Jordan. At the Para Asian Games in Nagoya, she brought glory to the country by winning bronze in the women's singles Class 6 table tennis event. Prachi has undergone six surgeries and can stand only with the support of a stick. Suhas LY: IAS officer and Paralympic medallist wins bronze Suhas LY, a 2007-batch IAS officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre, has served as District Magistrate of Azamgarh, Noida and Prayagraj. He is currently Secretary in the Department of Sports and Youth Welfare. He won silver at the 2020 Paralympics and another silver at the 2024 Paralympics. He has now added a bronze medal at the Asian Games to his achievements. Suhas is not only an accomplished athlete but also a major source of motivation for fellow competitors. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath often mentions his achievements. Originally from Karnataka, Suhas joined the IAS in 2007. Praveen Kumar: Turns a physical challenge into strength, wins gold Praveen Kumar, who hails from Govindgarh in Gautam Buddh Nagar, was born in 2003. His family was worried when they learnt that his left leg had a disability. As he grew older, he began walking with a limp. Praveen turned this challenge into his strength. He competed at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics and surprised everyone by winning silver in the high jump. He created history at the 2024 Paris Paralympics by winning gold. At the Para Asian Games in Japan, he once again claimed gold with a jump of 2.5 metres. Praveen has won medals at most of the events he has participated in. Swati Chaudhary: Husband quits job to support her sporting dream Swati Chaudhary's life is nothing short of extraordinary. In 2017, she developed paralysis in her legs following a caesarean delivery. Medical examinations revealed that she had transverse myelitis, a condition that affects the spinal cord and can impair movement in the lower half of the body. Swati underwent treatment for four years. Her husband, Gaurav Chaudhary, a software engineer by profession, left his job to care for her and encouraged her to take up archery. The Para Asian Games in Japan was the biggest event of Swati's career so far. She produced an outstanding performance to win silver in the W1 category. Before this, no Indian archer had won a medal in this category at the Asian Para Games. Gaurav's support played a crucial role in her achievement. Ram Ratan Singh: Returns to sport after a severe road accident, wins silver Ram Ratan Singh from Mathura suffered a serious road accident in 2017, sustaining a severe cervical spine injury. Before the accident, he used to play wrestling and cricket, but his injury forced him to give up both sports. However, Ram Ratan refused to lose hope and trained himself for discus throw. He won silver in the discus throw event at the Asian Games, securing his first Asian medal for the country. Pradeep Kumar: Wins silver in javelin throw Pradeep Kumar from Ghaziabad delivered an impressive performance in the javelin throw, recording a distance of 27.45 metres to win silver. His performance reflects his consistency. He had also won silver at the 2022 Asian Games.

stories.title: Akhilesh to decide tickets based on reports from 10 strategists:PDA panchayats held in every constituency to gather feedback
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance has not yet been finalised. Congress is demanding 140 seats, while the Samajwadi Party is unwilling to offer more than 70. A decision on seat-sharing is expected by 15 November. Even before that, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has begun searching for winnable candidates for more than 300 seats. Under the PDA formula, he has assigned responsibilities to 10 senior party leaders. They have been asked to attend PDA Panchayats in their respective assembly constituencies, assess the public mood and submit reports to Akhilesh Yadav. These reports will then be discussed with local MPs, district presidents and senior party functionaries before candidates are finalised. These reports will play three key roles in selecting candidates ahead of the 2027 elections: 1. They will identify the strongest candidates in each region and expose claims by those whose chances of winning are slight. 2. They will reveal what people think about each constituency and the factors they are likely to consider while voting. 3. They will help determine whether the potential candidates the SP is preparing for the election can actually win. Akhilesh is also ensuring that the PDA panchayats being held across Uttar Pradesh are not merely symbolic events. An example was seen in Kannauj. On 18 October, a PDA panchayat was held in the presence of state president Shyamlal Pal. After failing to draw a crowd, district president Kaleem Khan and all other office-bearers were removed. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav dissolved the entire district executive committee. Following this incident, office-bearers across districts have been meeting people, listening to their grievances and noting their suggestions. They are highlighting areas where BJP candidates have failed to deliver and reminding voters of the development work carried out in their areas during the SP government. They are also raising awareness about checking names on voter lists. Senior leaders are being assigned responsibilities through letters sent from the party's state headquarters. They have been asked to prepare reports on the Assembly constituencies where they have influence and submit them to the Lucknow headquarters. Meet the 10 leaders assigned responsibilities The SP has frequently faced accusations of being a party focused primarily on Yadavs. Ahead of the election, Akhilesh has brought forward influential leaders from non-Yadav OBC communities. The strategy is aimed at making inroads into the BJP's OBC vote bank, particularly among Kurmis, Mauryas/Kushwahas, Rajbhars, Nishads and Lodhs. 1. Non-Yadav OBCs Babu Singh Kushwaha: Has a strong presence among the Maurya, Kushwaha, Shakya and Saini communities. Ram Achal Rajbhar: A prominent Rajbhar leader, tasked with countering the influence of Om Prakash Rajbhar. Vishambhar Prasad Nishad: Has a strong base among the Nishad, Kashyap, Mallah and Bind communities. He is being positioned as an alternative to Sanjay Nishad. Ravindra Pratap Verma: Has a strong support base among Kurmis and is expected to counter Anupriya Patel's influence. 2. Dalit voters Awadhesh Prasad: A prominent Pasi leader who put the SP's PDA strategy in the national spotlight by winning the Ayodhya (Faizabad) Lok Sabha seat in the 2024 elections. Indrajeet Saroj: A former BSP leader with a strong presence among Pasi and other Dalit communities. He has considerable influence in eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Awadh region. Daddoo Prasad: A prominent Dalit leader in Bundelkhand and a veteran of the grassroots Bahujan movement. Ramji Lal Suman: Has a strong Dalit support base in western Uttar Pradesh. 3. Muslim community Nasimuddin Siddiqui: Was one of the BSP's most prominent Muslim leaders. His role is intended to strengthen the Muslim-Dalit combination across western Uttar Pradesh and the state as a whole, reinforce the SP's PDA strategy and convey the message that Muslims are respected in the party. Jasmeer Ansari: After leaving the BSP and joining the SP, Akhilesh appointed him Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council. He is believed to have a strong following among the Ansari community, whose population and electoral influence are considered significant in Uttar Pradesh. 4. Jat and farmer vote bank Harendra Malik: The MP from Muzaffarnagar and a senior Jat leader in western Uttar Pradesh. He is expected to help maintain the Jat-Muslim-Dalit combination in the region and compensate for the losses caused by Jayant Chaudhary's RLD joining the BJP-led alliance. (These leaders have been asked to stay connected with people and remind them of the development work carried out between 2012 and 2017, during the SP government.) Akhilesh expands the PDA base in western UP Akhilesh Yadav is working to expand the SP's base in western Uttar Pradesh. On 26 October, he inducted Rajpal Saini and Dara Singh Prajapati from Muzaffarnagar into the party. Sinod Shakya and Kushagra Sagar from Badaun also joined the SP. On 28 October, former MP Dharmendra Kashyap, a prominent Kashyap community leader from Bareilly, joined the party. The process of inducting new leaders is continuing. 'The SP will contest the 2027 election on caste equations' Political analyst Rajendra Kumar says caste remains the biggest factor determining electoral victories and defeats in Uttar Pradesh. The SP benefited in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from its PDA strategy and the narrative that the Constitution was under threat. Its vote share rose to 33.59% in 2024, compared with 18.11% in 2019, when it contested in alliance with the BSP. This represented an increase of 15.48 percentage points. New formula for every Assembly constituency More than 50 PDA panchayats have been held so far. Earlier, party leaders used these gatherings mainly to deliver election speeches. They have now been instructed to focus on local issues instead. The party does not want to impose a single formula across the state. It is therefore preparing separate manifestos for each Assembly constituency and district. State president Shyam Lal Pal is personally attending several of these panchayats. Separate plans have been drawn up for PDA panchayats in different regions. Eastern UP: Rajbhar, Nishad, Kurmi and Muslim voters play a decisive role here. The BJP has relied on the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), the Nishad Party and Apna Dal (S) to reach these communities. Akhilesh wants panchayats in the region to focus on the problems faced by Rajbhar, Nishad, Patel and Muslim voters and explain possible solutions. Awadh region: Non-Jatav Dalits, Yadavs, Kurmis and other backward classes are key voter groups here. Kurmi voters shifted towards the SP in 2024, creating several favourable electoral equations. The challenge this time is to retain their support while bringing new voter groups into the party's fold. Bundelkhand: The region faces problems related to drought, farming and canal irrigation. Many farmers belong to Dalit and backward communities. PDA panchayats here are focusing on these issues. Western UP: PDA panchayats are also being held among Jat and Gurjar communities that have traditionally supported the BJP. Discussions are tailored to the concerns of each community, while Muslim and Dalit voters remain a key focus. Victory or defeat was decided by just 1,000–5,000 votes in 38 seats In the 2022 Assembly elections, the margin of victory or defeat was between 1,000 and 5,000 votes in 38 constituencies. In 14 of these seats, the margin was just 1,000–2,000 votes. A private agency working for the SP is analysing these constituencies to determine the influence of different caste groups at each polling booth, where votes were split and where the party failed to secure vote transfers. Top 10 seats where the SP lost by very narrow margins SP spokesperson says party is fighting to protect constitutional rights, not for power SP national spokesperson Dr Ashutosh Verma says party leaders will travel from village to village to tell people the truth. stories.title: MBBS seniors force junior to perform obscene acts:17 medical college students suspended, fined ₹25,000 each
stories.summary: Seventeen MBBS students in Jalaun have been suspended for three months for ragging. A fine of ₹25,000 has also been imposed on each of them. On 21 October, MBBS students from the 2025 batch at the Government Medical College called their junior classmates to a room at 9 p.m. and ragged them there. A video of the ragging surfaced on 24 October. Following this, the college administration conducted an investigation and suspended seven students for one week. A fine of ₹1,000 was also imposed on each student. The college administration then expanded the investigation. The involvement of 10 more students came to light, taking the number of accused students to 17. The case falls under the jurisdiction of Orai Kotwali. How the ragging was carried out At the Government Medical College, senior students called junior students from the 2026 batch to a room on 21 October. There, they were first made to squat like chickens and forced to keep their heads down. They were then made to perform obscene acts. They were ragged with their hands held above their heads. At around 9 p.m. on 24 October, a student made a video of the ragging go viral. In it, senior students were seen locking the juniors in a room, abusing them and harassing them. After this, Principal Dr Arvind Trivedi and the college administration formed a team to investigate. It said that during the suspension period, the students would be barred from attending classes, staying in the hostel and performing clinical duties. Action to be taken for asking for mobile numbers too The college administration put up an office notice on 21 October to prevent ragging. It stated that asking junior students for their mobile numbers or forcing them to share their numbers is punishable under the anti-ragging rules. A warning was also issued that action would be taken against students who send messages to junior students. On Tuesday, Principal Dr Arvind Trivedi directed staff to strictly follow the instructions issued earlier. Junior students were instructed not to share their mobile numbers under pressure from any senior. If they receive an inappropriate message from a senior, they should block the number. They should also inform the anti-ragging committee. Action will also be taken against students who send or forward such messages. Helpline numbers put up in the hostel Principal Dr Arvind Trivedi said that the anti-ragging committee is active at the medical college. Essential contact numbers have been put up in the hostel to help students, enabling them to contact the authorities immediately in case of any problem.

stories.title: BSF jawan attacks judge in Agra:Father and gunner beaten, crowd smashes car window; tries to set it on fire
stories.summary: In Agra, a BSF jawan attacked the Additional District Judge (ADJ) of Aligarh. He summoned 30-40 associates. The judge, his father and his gunner were then assaulted. The attackers smashed the rear windscreen of the judge's car. The BSF jawan is accused of also trying to kill the judge's family and setting the car on fire. The incident took place on 24 October. The matter came to light after an FIR was registered on Tuesday. Police registered a case against BSF jawan Bhupendra and 40 unidentified people. Now read the full case Additional District Judge Ali Mustafa, posted at Court No. 5 in Aligarh, was travelling to Lucknow by car on Saturday, 24 October. His father, Ghulam Mustafa, mother and gunner were also in the car. After exiting the Yamuna Expressway at the Khandoli interchange, they reached the Agra-Aligarh route. In front of Jawahar Inter College at May crossroads, a motorcyclist collided with the driver's side of their car. The car was damaged. The judge asked his driver to stop the car and got out himself. He advised the motorcyclist to drive properly. However, the motorcyclist took offence and began abusing him. He identified himself as Bhupendra, a resident of Govindpur. He said, "I am a BSF soldier." He then called 30-40 people. Called 112, but received no police assistance A crowd gathered at the spot after the BSF jawan called them. The people began assaulting the judge's father and gunner. His father suffered injuries to his nose and the wrists of both hands. Fearing a major incident, the car was somehow moved out of the area. Bhupendra broke the rear windscreen by hitting it with a helmet or some other object. The Additional District Judge informed 112, but no assistance arrived at the spot. He informed the station house officer about the incident over the phone. Based on the complaint, police registered an FIR against Bhupendra, a resident of Govindpur in Hathras, and 40 unidentified people. DCP says: Accused being identified DCP Western Zone Aditya said that a case had been registered against 40 unidentified people. The accused are being identified on the basis of CCTV footage. The ADJ had informed the police by calling 112, but no help reached the spot. He then called the station house officer and informed him about the entire incident. He managed to escape from there somehow.

SP leader beats shopkeeper over ₹500, vandalises shop:Retired as an ASP; Akhilesh had inducted him into the party
stories.summary: In Gonda, a shopkeeper has accused retired ASP and Samajwadi Party leader Mahendra Kumar of assaulting him and vandalising his shop. He said Mahendra Kumar attacked him with sticks, smashed the computer and glass items kept in the shop, and threatened to kill him while brandishing a weapon. Mahendra Kumar recently joined the Samajwadi Party. He had retired as an ASP. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav inducted him into the party. The shopkeeper lodged a complaint at Nagar Kotwali at around 7 p.m. on Tuesday. Police said a dispute over a ₹500 transaction had come to light. The matter is being investigated. Dispute over printing cards for Sardar Patel Jayanti Surendra Gupta, who lives in Boodhadevar and owns a printing press and Lokvani centre, said, "Mahendra Kumar had given us the cards to print for the Sardar Patel Jayanti programme." At around 4 p.m. on Tuesday evening, his people arrived at the shop to collect the cards. I asked them to pay the ₹500 they owed me. The people who had come to the shop then had Mahendra Kumar speak to me over the phone. Attacked with sticks and sharp weapons Surendra Gupta alleges that Mahendra Kumar abused him over the phone. Shortly afterwards, Mahendra himself arrived at his shop with his associates. When he protested, they attacked and beat him with sticks and sharp weapons. They pointed a firearm at him and threatened to kill him. Outpost in-charge accused of removing CCTV camera Surendra Gupta also accused the outpost in-charge at Soni Gumti of removing the CCTV camera installed in the shop and taking it away. An attempt was made to contact Samajwadi Party leader Mahendra Kumar for his response in the matter. However, he did not answer the phone or respond to the WhatsApp message. stories.title: Criminal carrying ₹1 lakh bounty killed in Etah:Police shot him in the chest; he had robbed a jeweller five days earlier
stories.summary: Police killed wanted criminal Virendra, carrying a ₹1 lakh reward, in an encounter in Etah. Virendra was shot in the chest during the firing. His accomplice used the darkness to escape. A police officer was injured in the encounter. Police recovered a pistol, cartridges and a stolen motorcycle from the spot. A search is under way for the absconding criminal. The encounter took place at 6 p.m. on Tuesday in the Kotwali Pilua area. Jeweller had been robbed According to the police, Virendra had robbed jeweller Sanjay Yadav in Aliganj, Etah. Sanjay owns a shop named Maa Saraswati Jewellers in Mewati Mohalla. On 22 October, the criminals looted 10 kg of silver, 250 grams of gold and ₹1 lakh from the shop. Police had deployed six teams to arrest the criminals. On 25 October, ADG Agra Zone SK Bhagat announced a reward of ₹1 lakh for Virendra. 53 cases registered; Virendra was a resident of Mainpuri Virendra was originally a resident of Harchandpur in Mainpuri district. Fifty-two cases were registered against him in several districts. His brother also has 25 cases registered against him. Moreover, Virendra's wife has also served time in jail in a robbery case. She was accused of shooting and killing a woman in Mainpuri. According to the police, Virendra stole a motorcycle in Unnao on 21 October. The same motorcycle was used the following day in the robbery of a jeweller in Aliganj. Encounter near Sunna Canal at 6 p.m. SSP Dr Ilamaran said that a reward of ₹1 lakh had been announced for Virendra. The police had been searching for him. On Tuesday evening, he was seen travelling on a motorcycle with his accomplice. When the police team tried to stop Virendra, he opened fire. The police fired back. One bullet hit Virendra in the chest, causing him to fall. His accomplice, however, took advantage of the darkness and escaped. Injured Virendra was taken to the medical college, where doctors declared him dead. Constable Satyapal, who was injured in the encounter, has also been admitted to the medical college. He is undergoing treatment. Police examined footage from 1,000 CCTV cameras Police examined footage from around 1,000 CCTV cameras to identify and trace the criminals who robbed the jeweller. They were then searching for the suspects with the help of surveillance. Story being updated

stories.title: Varanasi poster depicts Mayawati as Goddess Durga:Shows her with eight arms holding scales and the Constitution, declares she will become CM
stories.summary: A poster depicting Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national president and former Chief Minister Mayawati as Goddess Durga has become a topic of discussion at the district headquarters in Varanasi. The poster shows Mayawati as an eight-armed goddess riding a lion. It was put up by local leader Ashutosh Pathak. Through the poster, he has expressed his wish to see Mayawati become Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister once again. Mayawati depicted as an eight-armed goddess riding a lion The large hoarding installed on a pole at the district headquarters shows Mayawati riding a lion. Different symbols have been depicted in her eight hands, including the Constitution of India, the scales of justice, books representing education and a media microphone. The poster also highlights six key areas, including the Constitution, justice, media, education, health and industry. Through these, it seeks to convey a message of building a clean, safe and educated Uttar Pradesh. Ashutosh Pathak expresses desire to make Mayawati chief minister Ashutosh Pathak, who had the poster put up, is shown with folded hands in a photograph at the bottom of it. The hoarding reads: "I wish to make Maiya Mayawati chief minister of Uttar Pradesh; I wish to make Uttar Pradesh clean, safe and educated." Poster put up above the SP MLC's banner A banner belonging to Ashutosh Sinha, a Samajwadi Party (SP) member of the Legislative Council, has also been put up directly above this poster. As a result, banners of leaders associated with different political parties can be seen together at the district headquarters. The poster depicting Mayawati in the form of a goddess has become a subject of political discussion. While it is being viewed as an attempt by a BSP supporter to convey a message in support of Mayawati, questions may also be raised about the political use of religious symbols.

stories.title: Man killed friend over money for alcohol in Lucknow:Stabbed him in the neck, police arrest suspect carrying ₹25,000 bounty
stories.summary: A man slit his friend's throat with a knife and killed him during a dispute over money for alcohol in Lucknow's Krishnanagar. Fearing he would be caught, the accused dumped the body on a rubbish heap outside his house after the incident. Police arrested the absconding accused, Rajesh Rawat alias Kali, who carried a reward of ₹25,000, on Tuesday. They also recovered the knife used in the murder. Murder was committed 18 days ago According to police, Jaya Devi, a resident of Kotra village in the Tadiyawan police station area of Hardoi, lodged an FIR at Krishnanagar police station on 9 October in connection with the murder of her son, Sukhpal, 27. After the case was registered, four police teams began searching for the accused. As he could not be traced, a reward of ₹25,000 was announced for information leading to his arrest. With the help of surveillance and manual evidence, police arrested the accused on Tuesday. He was identified as Rajesh Rawat alias Kali, a resident of Mamresh in Unnao. Dispute occurred while drinking alcohol During questioning, accused Rajesh said that he and Sukhpal were friends. They lived in a rented room in the Krishnanagar area and worked as labourers. After work on 8 October, they reached the room with alcohol. While they were drinking together, an argument broke out over payment of the money. During the argument, Sukhpal began hurling abuses. In a fit of anger, Rajesh attacked him in the neck with a knife lying nearby, killing him. Fearing that he would be caught, he dumped Sukhpal's body on the rubbish outside the house.

stories.title: Blue drum murder case:Allahabad HC to hear Muskan, Sahil's death penalty appeals on Nov 30
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Tuesday admitted appeals filed by Sahil Shukla and Muskan Rastogi challenging their conviction in the Meerut blue drum murder case. The next hearing was scheduled for November 30. A division bench of Justices Padam Narayan Mishra and Salil Kumar Rai heard the appeals. The two convicts challenged the Meerut trial court sentencing them to death for murdering Saurabh Rajput. Questions remain over the custody of Muskan's daughter. Jail senior superintendent., Meerut, Viresh Raj Sharma said Muskan's wishes are going to be important in finalising whom the child is handed over to. Sharma said, “If the family of Sahil wants to take responsibility for the girl, it must submit an application to the jail's administration. Then the request will be placed before Muskan. Further action will be taken in accordance to her wishes.” He added that a Mumbai-based social media influencer has offered to bear expenses of raising Muskan's daughter. Muskan has declined the offer. Both convicts have moved the High Court through the same lawyer. This has prompted speculation on whether Sahil's family has accepted Muskan. Earlier, Muskan sought legal representation through the jail's administration. Sahil's family had appointed a lawyer to challenge the death sentence. The same lawyer subsequently had filed an appeal on behalf of Muskan. Sharma, however, said he could not say whether Sahil's family accepted Muskan. During the trial, Muskan was provided a government lawyer, Rekha Jain. Her family had distanced itself from her. Sahil was represented by a lawyer chosen by his family. The case is on the murder of Saurabh Rajput, the husband of Muskan. As per the prosecution, Saurabh's dismembered remains were hidden in a blue drum which was filled with cement. A trial court in Meerut convicted Sahil and Muskan. They were sentenced to death (October 14, 2026).

stories.title: ‘Destroy the killers’ families,’ mother says seeing husband, son dead:Deputy CM carries their bodies on his shoulder, government promises her a job
stories.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak shouldered the bodies of the victims of the broad-daylight triple murder in Lucknow. He announced that the mother would be given a government job, the girl's education would be free, and the family would receive security. Action would be taken against the accused under the National Security Act (NSA). After these assurances, the family members allowed the three bodies to be taken away. The three funeral biers were lifted five hours later. The last rites will be performed at Gulala Ghat. When the bodies of the father, son and younger brother reached home after the post-mortem, the mother and sister began wailing hysterically at the sight of them. The mother had said while crying, "The killer has destroyed our family. He should be hanged. The house should be demolished with a bulldozer. Finish off his family too." At around 3 p.m., Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak, Mayor Sushma Kharakwal and BJP state vice-president Neeraj Singh reached the victims' home. During this, people raised slogans loudly in front of him. They kept chanting slogans such as "Bulldozer rule has fallen asleep", while the Deputy Chief Minister went to the victims' homes with folded hands in silence. Municipal corporation and district administration officials were already present there. The police took action in the case and suspended the inspector and the outpost in-charge. Three people were killed in a dispute over car parking and a raised platform On Monday morning, Rishabh Shukla (30) shot dead three people in Saadatganj's Brahmin Tola over a dispute involving car parking and a raised platform. One of the victims, Shivaji Tiwari (62), was a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the RSS district sarkaryavah. Shivaji's brother, Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Shivaji's son Suyash (30) ran an electrical goods business. He was due to get married on 5 December. The accused, Rishabh, was a navigation officer in the Merchant Navy.

stories.title: Lawyer and two companions fired at in Lucknow’s Madiaon:Car windows smashed with sticks; attackers accused of snatching gold chain from his neck
stories.summary: A lawyer and his two associates were attacked in Lucknow's Madiyaon on Monday night. Sharif, the owner of Janta Doodh Dairy, opened fire at them along with three unidentified accomplices. The attackers smashed the car windows with sticks and robbed the lawyer of a chain from his neck. A video of the incident has also emerged. In a complaint filed with the police, advocate Dharmendra Kumar Singh Somvanshi, a resident of Loharamau in Faizullaganj, said that at around 9 p.m. on Tuesday, he was returning from the High Court with fellow advocates Abhinay Singh and Ankit Purwal. As they reached the Maurya Market intersection, the accused, who had been lying in wait, attacked them. See two pictures... They smashed the car window after beating them with sticks According to Dharmendra, the accused opened fire with illegal firearms and smashed the windows of his car with sticks. They then snatched the chain around his neck. The attackers allegedly fled the spot while firing with the intention of killing him. The victim said he and his companions saved their lives by hiding inside the car. The car was damaged in the attack. He and his companions have been frightened since the incident. The victim claimed to have identified the accused. Madiyaon Inspector Alok Rao said the dispute at the dairy was over rabri. It then escalated into a scuffle. The accused vandalised the vehicle, and one person has been taken into custody.

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya’s wife fears being framed under Arms Act:Claims husband has her three firearms; Pratapgarh police sends her notice
stories.summary: Strongman MLA Raja Bhaiya's wife, Bhanvi Singh, on Tuesday expressed apprehension that preparations were under way to implicate her in a case under the Arms Act. She wrote on X at 2 p.m. that two allegedly false FIRs had been registered against her at Lucknow's Hazratganj police station and that a charge sheet had also been filed. The Pratapgarh administration has now sent her a notice under the Arms Act. Bhanvi expressed apprehension that preparations might be under way to implicate her in yet another case. In the post, Bhanvi Singh tagged several officials, including those from the Uttar Pradesh Police, Lucknow Police and Pratapgarh Police. She demanded an impartial investigation into the matter and action in accordance with the law. 'An FIR was registered; I found out through the media' Bhanvi claimed that an FIR was registered against her in 2024 at Hazratganj police station during the tenure of then SHO Vikram Singh. Her child was also named in it. She said she learnt about the FIR from media personnel. In her post, she wrote that when she asked then DCP Ravina Tyagi about the FIR, Tyagi denied having any knowledge of it. Bhanvi questioned why senior officers were not informed that an FIR had been registered at the police station and who was accountable for this. Bhanvi alleged that statements were recorded in her name that she had never made. She said that when she asked the investigating officers about the status of the FIR, she did not receive satisfactory information. Later, after approaching the court, she learnt that a chargesheet had been filed and received information about the further investigation. 'I received a notice instead of weapons being recovered' Bhanvi Singh has also complained in her post about the licensed weapons. She claims that since 2023, she has been complaining that licensed weapons registered in her name are in her husband's possession. Despite this, instead of recovering the weapons, the Pratapgarh administration sent her a notice under the Arms Act. She said she had nothing to do with the weapons, ammunition or any illegal activity. According to her, the licensed weapons have been out of her custody for a long time, and she herself has been filing complaints seeking their recovery. "Why am I being asked to explain myself instead of action being taken on my complaints?" Bhanvi alleged that instead of acting on her complaints, she was repeatedly being put in a position where she had to explain herself. Referring to the actions of the Nainital, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh police, she expressed fears of mental harassment and retaliatory action. She tagged the Uttar Pradesh Police, the DGP, the Lucknow Police Commissionerate, the Pratapgarh Police, the Chief Minister's Office, the National Commission for Women and other concerned institutions, seeking action. Bhanvi said she wanted only a fair investigation, justice and respectful treatment in accordance with the law. She questioned why she had to repeatedly explain herself for seeking her safety and justice.

stories.title: Groom skips wedding over demand for Thar:Bride faints in Gonda; mother says he used to stay at their home for 15 days at a time
stories.summary: In Gonda, the groom did not arrive with the wedding procession because he was not given a Thar as part of the marriage. The bride and her family waited for the wedding party throughout the night. The groom did not agree even after repeated attempts to persuade him. He refused to go ahead with the wedding without the vehicle. The bride, who was dressed in her wedding attire and waiting for the ceremony, was left traumatised and fainted several times while crying. Her condition deteriorated, and she was admitted to hospital. On Tuesday morning, the family submitted a complaint at the police station against the groom and his family, demanding action. The matter concerns the Nagar Kotwali area. Now, read the full story Mirza Ajmal Beg, a resident of Katariya locality, works as a driver. His family includes his wife, Nazo Khatun, daughter Naushba Mirza Beg and a son. About a year ago, Ajmal arranged Naushba's nikah with Mohammed Salman, the son of Mohammed Aslam, who lives in Gorakhpur. Salman is the eldest of three brothers and one sister. He is currently studying abroad. The nikah was scheduled for Monday, 26 October. A marriage palace in the city had been booked for the ceremony. The bride had applied mehndi to her hands and was dressed and waiting for the wedding. Relatives were also waiting for the wedding procession to arrive. When the wedding procession did not arrive even after the scheduled time had passed, the bride's family called the groom's relatives. For a long time, the groom's family kept putting them off, saying that the wedding procession was about to leave. They kept waiting until 6 a.m. The bride's mother, Nazo Khatun, said that after midnight, the groom's family made it clear that the wedding would not take place if a THAR was not given as dowry. As soon as she heard that the wedding procession would not arrive and that the relationship had ended, her daughter fainted and lost consciousness. We admitted her to hospital. Mother said: Groom used to stay at our home for 15 days Mother Nazo Khatun said, "After the marriage was fixed, the prospective groom frequently visited our home. He would stay at our house for 15 days at a time. Initially, the groom and his family had said that they did not want anything. They only asked us to solemnise the nikah simply. We told them that we had only one daughter and would give a motorbike as dowry according to our means. They agreed at the time." The mother said that the elders in their family folded their hands and pleaded with the groom's family, but they remained adamant about their demand and refused to go ahead with the wedding. City Kotwal Bindeshwari Mani Tripathi said that the police reached the spot and asked the family for the full details. The groom's family is also being contacted.

stories.title: Students cause chaos in Prayagraj, smash chairs:Break through four layers of barricades to enter education directorate, clash with police
stories.summary: Prayagraj witnessed chaotic scenes on Tuesday afternoon as students protesting for the TGT-PGT recruitment launched an agitation. At around 3 pm, nearly 200 students breached a four-layer barricade to forcibly enter the Directorate of Education. They attempted to lock up various offices, damaged several chairs, and shouted slogans after entering the corridors. Following this, they staged a sit-in protest within the premises. The students had been protesting in front of the Directorate since Monday, raising slogans against the government and officials. Demonstrators chanted slogans such as "Restore the old manual" and "Give us one opportunity". Issuing a warning, the students stated that the protest would not end until a solid and written decision regarding their demands is taken. Prior to this, TGT-PGT aspirants had staged a sit-in protest at Patthar Girjaghar from 5 to 23 September 2026, opposing the new recruitment manual and demanding the restoration of the old manual. The 19-day-long hunger strike was called off after the district administration provided assurances and offered juice to the protesters. The Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission has advertised 17,735 TGT posts. Online applications are being accepted from 24 October to 23 November.

stories.title: Former BJP MP Dharmendra Kashyap joins SP:Quit BJP saying ‘Tata-bye-bye’; Akhilesh inducts 20 leaders into party
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party is expanding its political base. On October 27, Akhilesh Yadav inducted former BJP MP Dharmendra Kashyap, who represented Aonla in Bareilly, and his daughter Kirti Kashyap into the party. Earlier, after resigning from the BJP, Dharmendra Kashyap met Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on October 11 along with his daughter. Since then, speculation about his joining the SP had intensified. Along with former MP Dharmendra Kashyap, several prominent leaders and workers from various parties joined the SP: Aonla (Bareilly): Former SP candidate Syed Abid Ali, Kirti Kashyap and Faheemuddin, the chairman. Shravasti: Dev Pratap Singh, Tej Pratap Singh and Ranjeet Giri Goswami. Bahraich: Santosh Tiwari and Pankaj Kumar Verma. Unnao: Sarvesh Kumar Verma. Other leaders who came from the BJP: Anand Sahu, Dr Pramod, Vilas Babu Valmiki, Adhikar Singh, Shyam Sundar Valmiki, Suresh Valmiki, Suresh Suraj Pal, Vijay Chauhan, Guru Prasad and Prem Rathore. Upset with BJP for not being nominated to Rajya Sabha Dharmendra Kashyap was elected MP from the Aonla constituency on a BJP ticket in 2014 and 2019. He lost the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Since then, he had been upset over being sidelined by the party and the lack of action against those accused of working against BJP candidates during the election. After he was not nominated for the Rajya Sabha in the election held in October, he announced his decision to quit the BJP through a social media post saying, ‘Tata, bye-bye’. Started his political journey with BSP Dharmendra Kashyap began his political career in 2002 by winning the Sanha Assembly seat on a BSP ticket. He later joined the SP and became a Minister of State in the Mulayam Singh government in 2003. He was elected MLA again in 2007. Just before the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, he joined the BJP and became an MP. He has now returned to the SP. Daughter likely to contest from Bithri Chainpur The SP is widely expected to give a ticket to former MP Dharmendra Kashyap’s daughter, Kirti Kashyap. She may contest from the Bithri Chainpur Assembly seat in Bareilly. Akhilesh says BJP has resorted to dishonesty Akhilesh said, “The three prominent faces who contested against one another in the 2024 election in Aonla—Dharmendra Kashyap, Neeraj Maurya and Syed Abid Ali—are now sharing the same stage. “When Dharmendra ji said ‘Tata, bye-bye’ while leaving the BJP, we had wanted him to join us ever since. His arrival will further strengthen our fight for social justice. Our party will leave no stone unturned to give him full political respect and the right place. “The truth is that the BJP will lose the moment the election dates are announced. Fearing this defeat, it is being forced to resort to dishonesty and manipulation.” What other SP leaders said about the party's growing strength Shivpal Singh Yadav: A change in Uttar Pradesh is inevitable. People are troubled by inflation, corruption, bulldozer action and fake encounters. Every section of society is facing injustice. Small traders are being extorted, and the budget is being looted. Social justice will be ensured for everyone only under Akhilesh Yadav's leadership. Dharmendra Kashyap: Law and order in Uttar Pradesh has been held hostage, and backward classes are not getting justice. Bulldozers are not being used against those who kill members of the Kashyap community. I assure you that I will bring every single member of the fishing community into the SP fold. “Development is stuck, law and order is held hostage. The people of UP say Akhilesh is the need of the hour.” Neeraj Maurya (Aonla MP): Today is a historic day for Aonla. The three leaders who contested the 2024 elections from three different parties are now sharing the same stage. We will strengthen the SP in 2027 and make Akhilesh Yadav the Chief Minister.

stories.title: Bulldozer demolishes home of accused in Lucknow triple murder:Deputy CM shoulders victims’ coffins; victim’s mother urges authorities to "eliminate the killers"
stories.summary: Chaos broke out on Tuesday following a daylight triple murder in Lucknow. As the bodies of the father, son, and brother arrived home after the post-mortem, residents blocked the road. Meanwhile, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak also reached the deceaseds' residence. Upon seeing him, people raised slogans such as "Bulldozer governance has gone to sleep". However, the Deputy Chief Minister quietly walked inside the house with folded hands to meet the family. Following this, the Deputy Chief Minister announced that Ruchi Tiwari, wife of Shivendra Tiwari alias Shambhu, would be given a government job. The daughter's education will be free for life. The family will be provided with security. Action under the National Security Act (NSA) will be taken against the accused. Within six hours of the Deputy Chief Minister's announcement, at 10 pm, the Lucknow Development Authority's (LDA) bulldozer was deployed at the murderer's house. In the evening, LDA officials sealed his residence, after which the boundary wall began to be demolished with the bulldozer at night. Prior to this, belongings were removed and taken out from the houses of the accused's uncle and other family members. Following the Deputy Chief Minister's assurance, the family agreed to take the three bodies for the final rites. The Deputy Chief Minister also carried the bier on his shoulder and placed wood on the pyre. Nearly 5 hours after the post-mortem, all three bodies were cremated at Gulala Ghat. Earlier, when the bodies of the father, son, and younger brother arrived home after the post-mortem, the mother and sister began weeping inconsolably upon seeing the corpses. The mother wept, saying, "The killer has devastated our family. He should be hanged. Destroy his family too." Meanwhile, Commissioner of Police Tarun Gaba suspended Saadatganj Police Station Inspector Santosh Kumar Arya and Outpost In-charge Ajay Kumar Chaurasia. Late in the evening, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) sealed the house of the murder accused, Rishabh Shukla. Meanwhile, the houses of his uncle Girish and others were being vacated until late at night. 3 people were murdered over a car parking and platform dispute In Saadatganj's Brahman Tola on Monday morning, Rishabh Shukla (30) shot and killed 3 people following a dispute over car parking and a platform (chabutara). The deceased, Shivaji Tiwari (62), was a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the RSS District General Secretary (Sar Karyavah). Shivaji's brother, Shivendra Tiwari alias Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Shivaji's son, Suyash (30), ran an electrical goods business. His wedding was scheduled for 5 December. The accused, Rishabh, was a navigation officer in the Merchant Navy.
