stories.title: UP govt to give poor families 100 chicks free:₹50,000 subsidy for buying a cow, free treatment worth ₹5 lakh for teaching staff; Cabinet clears 22 decisions
stories.summary: The Yogi government has decided to provide a subsidy of up to 50% on the purchase of cows. In addition, 100 chicks will be distributed free of cost to poor families to encourage poultry farming. At a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday, 22 proposals were approved. The Cabinet also approved new provisions for voter eligibility in panchayat elections. Now, a person must have been residing in a village for at least six months to be eligible to register as a voter. The Cabinet has also made it mandatory for fishermen and other individuals to register their boats and steamers. Read which 22 proposals were approved by the Cabinet… 1. Subsidy on cow purchases; 100 free chicks for poor families The State Livestock Mission will be launched to increase milk production, improve cattle breeds and boost the income of livestock farmers. Under the scheme, the government will pay 85% of the insurance premium for cows, while livestock farmers will contribute the remaining 15%. The government will provide a subsidy of up to 50% on purchasing cows from other states. This benefit will be limited to the purchase of two cows. For example, if a livestock farmer buys a cow for ₹50,000, the government will provide ₹25,000 as a subsidy. Minister Dharampal Singh said poor families would be given 100 chicks each free of cost to encourage poultry farming. 2. Six months of residence mandatory to register as a voter in panchayat elections For panchayat elections, a voter must have been residing in the village for at least six months. The Cabinet has approved an amendment to the relevant Act. Until now, the Act did not clearly specify who could qualify as a voter. Under the amendment, a person aged 18 or above who ordinarily resides in the village for six months or more will be eligible to be included in the panchayat electoral roll, on the lines of the Election Commission of India's electoral rolls. 3. Four government hospitals to operate under the PPP model The government has approved the operation of four hospitals under the public-private partnership (PPP) model: the 300-bed hospital in Bareilly, the 200-bed hospital in Banda, the 200-bed hospital in Tanda, Ambedkar Nagar, and the 200-bed hospital in Karvi, Chitrakoot. The plan is to provide the services of 12 specialist doctors and three super-specialist doctors at these hospitals. Treatment and outpatient department (OPD) charges will be in line with those at KGMU, Lucknow. Patients will also be able to receive treatment using Ayushman cards at these hospitals. 4. Registration mandatory for boats and steamers operating on rivers Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh said the Cabinet had approved the Uttar Pradesh Inland Vessel Rules. An Inland Water Authority will be established to oversee water transport, with the Transport Minister serving as its chairperson. He said registration would be mandatory for boats and steamers operating on 11 rivers in the state, including the Ganga, Yamuna, Saryu and Ghaghra. A registration fee of ₹50 has been fixed for non-passenger boats. In addition, both passengers and boat operators will be insured to improve safety and prevent accidents. 5. Prayagraj's SRN Hospital to have 3,000 beds Approval has been granted to increase the capacity of Prayagraj's Swaroop Rani Nehru (SRN) Hospital from 1,250 to 3,000 beds. Permission has also been granted to demolish old and dilapidated government buildings on the hospital premises in compliance with a High Court order. 6. Grain warehouses with a capacity of 65,000 metric tonnes to be built in Bundelkhand Large warehouses will be built in Jhansi and Lalitpur to ensure the safe storage of farmers' produce in Bundelkhand. Modern warehouses with capacities of 30,000 metric tonnes in Jhansi and 35,000 metric tonnes in Lalitpur will be developed. They will be able to store crops such as pulses, oilseeds, pearl millet and sorghum. 7. Sainik School Mainpuri to receive 9.524 hectares of land free of cost High-tension power lines passing through the Sainik School campus in Mainpuri had created difficulties for classes and hostel construction. In view of this, the government has approved the free transfer of 9.524 hectares (approximately 23 acres) of government land in Nauner village to the Ministry of Defence. The land will be used to expand the school and develop new hostels and other facilities. 8. Cashless treatment for 48,062 non-teaching employees in secondary education A total of 48,062 non-teaching employees of non-government aided, unaided and Sanskrit secondary schools, along with their families, will receive cashless medical treatment worth up to ₹5 lakh. The coverage includes inpatient treatment (IPD). The government will pay an annual insurance premium of ₹3,000 per employee. 9. Cashless treatment for 1.22 lakh non-teaching employees in basic education A total of 1,22,304 non-teaching employees of the Basic Education Council, aided junior high schools, unaided schools and the Samagra Shiksha project will also receive cashless treatment at government and private hospitals. The government will pay an annual insurance premium of ₹3,000 per employee for this facility. 10. Electronics plant in Greater Noida; five-star hotel to come up in Prayagraj Haier India will set up an electronics plant in Greater Noida at an investment of ₹1,271 crore. Meanwhile, Ekavo Hospitality will develop a five-star hotel with 158 rooms and a mall in Prayagraj at a cost of ₹654.61 crore. 11. Four companies to invest over ₹1,710 crore in Noida Investment proposals from four companies in Gautam Buddha Nagar have been approved under Uttar Pradesh's Global Capability Centre (GCC) policy. These include proposals worth ₹879 crore from Havells, ₹634 crore from LG Soft, ₹112.84 crore from Ameriprise and ₹84 crore from MetLife. These investments will help establish centres focused on IT, technology and research. 12. Stamp duty rules set for company mergers and demergers Stamp duty rates have been fixed for company mergers and demergers. Under the new arrangement, stamp duty of 0.50% will be charged on the value of shares and 2% in cases involving immovable property. The move is expected to simplify the process of corporate restructuring. 13. 845 new flats to be built for Allahabad High Court officials A total of 845 new Type-3 and Type-4 flats will be constructed for Class-I and Class-II officials of the Allahabad High Court at Devghat, Jhalwa, in Prayagraj. The project will cost ₹543.40 crore. 14. IIT Kanpur to establish Uttar Pradesh's Cyber Security Operations Centre The Uttar Pradesh Cyber Security Operations Centre (UP-CSOC) will be established through IIT Kanpur to protect government networks and applications from hacking, data theft and cyberattacks. The project will cost ₹104.28 crore. The centre will have round-the-clock monitoring facilities. 15. Textile park to be developed across 1,000 acres on the Lucknow-Hardoi border A textile park spanning 1,000 acres will be developed on the Lucknow-Hardoi border under the PM MITRA scheme. Ramky Infrastructure has been selected to construct and operate the park. The project will cost ₹1,947 crore and is expected to generate employment on a large scale. 16. Pragati Robotics Park to be developed in Greater Noida Pragati Robotics Park will be developed on approximately 70 acres of land in Greater Noida. It will provide facilities for companies working in robotics and artificial intelligence (AI). The project is expected to generate one lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities. 17. Working women's hostel and auditorium to be built in Prayagraj A 7,912-square-metre Nazul land parcel in the Kitab Ghar area near the Civil Station in Prayagraj will be transferred free of cost to the Municipal Corporation. A working women's hostel and an auditorium will be built on the land. 18. ₹2,900 crore approved for sewerage and drinking water projects in Lucknow and Varanasi Proposals worth ₹2,900 crore have been approved under the AMRUT 2.0 scheme to develop sewerage networks and drinking water facilities in Lucknow and Varanasi. Six projects involving sewerage networks and clean water pipelines will be implemented in the Trans Varuna, Lahartara and Chitaipur zones of Varanasi. These projects are expected to benefit around 16 lakh people. A drinking water project in the Keshari Kheda ward of the Haiderganj and Alamnagar areas of Lucknow will benefit 1.56 lakh people. 19. Solar plant in Yamuna Expressway region gets relief on bank guarantee Relief has been granted to the solar cell and module plant being established in the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) region at a cost of ₹8,253 crore. M/s SAEL Solar P-6 has been permitted to submit an insurance surety bond instead of a bank guarantee. This is expected to make it easier for the company to obtain financial assistance and loans. 20. Four new link expressways to be built at a cost of ₹17,542 crore The state government will build four new link expressways at a cost of ₹17,542 crore using its own resources. These include the Farrukhabad Link Expressway, a link connecting the Agra-Lucknow Expressway with the Purvanchal Expressway, the Jhansi Link Expressway and the Jewar Airport Link Expressway. The projects are expected to generate approximately 7.6 crore person-days of employment. 21. Approval granted to withdraw the Education Service Tribunal Bill, 2021 Certain provisions of the Education Service Tribunal Bill, 2021, which deals with the resolution of disputes involving teachers and employees, were not in line with central laws. In view of this, the government has decided to withdraw the Bill for amendments so that an improved framework can be introduced after the necessary changes. 22. Approval for policy proposals related to Ayush and other departments The Cabinet also approved various proposals related to Ayush education, regional development and local administrative procedures. These include proposals to amend the relevant rules.

stories.title: Govt nurse gets pregnant sister-in-law killed:Hired contract killer for ₹3 lakh in Deoria, fearing her affair would be exposed
stories.summary: A government nurse in Deoria got her pregnant sister-in-law murdered by a contract killer. Her sister-in-law was an obstacle to her affair. She had agreed to pay ₹3 lakh for the murder along with her lover. She pawned her jewellery and paid ₹2.5 lakh in advance to the killer. According to the police, acting on the nurse’s instructions, the accused entered her government accommodation with an accomplice and strangled her sister-in-law. He then struck her on the head with a hammer, killing her. The incident took place late on the night of October 24 in Rudrapur town, around 20 km from the district headquarters. After the murder, the nurse staged a scene and informed the police herself. Her family belongs to the Sahjanwa area of Gorakhpur, while she worked in Deoria. Initially, the victim’s mother filed an FIR against five members of her daughter’s in-laws’ family, including the nurse, alleging dowry murder. However, after the post-mortem report, the police grew suspicious of the nurse. During intense questioning, she confessed to arranging the murder for money. On Monday night, the police arrested one of the accused following an encounter. See the pictures... Know the full story... Gudiya (28), wife of Chaman Lal and a resident of Chandbari village in the Sahjanwan police station area of Gorakhpur district, had been living for some time in the government accommodation of her sister-in-law, Purnima. Gudiya was about five months pregnant. Due to a dispute with her husband, she was living in Rudrapur with her three-year-old daughter. Purnima was posted as a staff nurse at the Rudrapur Community Health Centre. She had been living for about five years in the government accommodation on the CHC premises. She was unmarried. During this period, she began an affair with a young man who lived nearby. The two often met at night. Gudiya learned about her sister-in-law's affair. She had seen the two of them together several times. She would say that she would tell the family about it. Purnima feared that her sister-in-law would inform the family about her affair. For this reason, she hatched a murder conspiracy with her lover. Lover put him in touch with a contract killer According to the police, Purnima's lover contacted a contract killer from Gorakhpur. A deal was finalised for ₹3 lakh to murder Gudiya. Of this, ₹2.5 lakh was paid in advance. On the night of 24 October, Gudiya was on the third floor of the government accommodation on the CHC premises. She and Purnima were sleeping in separate rooms. As part of the conspiracy, Purnima used an excuse to have Gudiya's three-year-old daughter sleep with her, while Gudiya was alone in the room. At around 11 p.m., Purnima called a contract killer. He arrived at the government accommodation with his associate. They entered the room and locked the door. They then strangled Gudiya with a rope and killed her by striking her on the head with a hammer. After the murder, both assailants fled. Purnima then raised the alarm about the murder and informed the police to avoid suspicion herself. SP also reached the scene at night On receiving the information, the police reached the scene. SP Abhijeet R. Shankar also inspected the crime scene. The police sent the body for a post-mortem examination. During this period, Gudiya's mother, Lalti Devi, created a commotion, accusing her in-laws of killing her for dowry. On the basis of her written complaint, police registered a case against her husband, Chaman Lal; mother-in-law Urmila Devi; sister-in-law Purnima Vishwakarma; elder brother-in-law Abhimanyu; and elder brother-in-law's wife, Bandevi. During the investigation, police detained Purnima, her husband, and some others for questioning. Suspicion deepens after post-mortem report According to police, the post-mortem report confirmed that the woman had died after being strangled and struck on the head. Based on Purnima's presence during the incident and other circumstances, police suspicion of her began to deepen. During intensive questioning, Purnima broke down and confessed to arranging the killing through a contract killer. Police then began searching for the contract killer. Meanwhile, they received information that the criminals were coming to collect the outstanding ₹50,000 owed by the nurse's lover. Police laid a cordon and arrested Ramashish Yadav after an encounter, while his accomplice escaped. Police are searching for him. According to police, when Purnima fell short of the money needed for the contract killing, she pawned her jewellery to raise the funds. SP Abhijeet R. Shankar said: “The nurse had arranged the murder by paying for a contract killing. She had already been taken into custody. The absconding criminal was arrested after an encounter. A case has been registered against nurse Purnima, her lover and the criminals.”

stories.title: Local passes at 135 UP toll plazas:Residents within 20 km to pay ₹1,500–₹3,000 yearly; new rules from Nov 1
stories.summary: Eligible private vehicle owners living within a 20-kilometre radius of a toll plaza will be able to obtain an annual local pass. They will have to pay ₹1,500 or ₹3,000 a year, depending on the prescribed category of the toll plaza. This will spare people who cross the toll plaza daily or frequently from paying separate toll charges on every journey. The Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways issued a notification amending the National Highway Fee Rules, 2008, on 26 October 2026. The rules will come into effect on 1 November 2026. According to the notification, the facility is available to eligible private vehicle owners who have a valid FASTag and live within the prescribed radius of the relevant toll plaza. The pass will be valid only at the relevant toll plaza. How will people in UP benefit? Uttar Pradesh has 135 NHAI toll plazas. This facility could benefit salaried employees, business owners and other private vehicle owners living near these toll plazas. It will particularly provide relief to those who have to cross toll plazas every day for work, education or other essential purposes. However, this pass will not be free for all vehicle owners or be valid uniformly across the state. It will be available only to those who meet the prescribed eligibility criteria and the conditions set by the concerned toll plaza. Who is eligible for the ₹1,500 and ₹3,000 rates? These conditions must be kept in mind The vehicle must be registered for private use, meaning it must not be a commercial vehicle. It must have a valid and active FASTag. The vehicle owner's residence must be within 20 kilometres of the concerned toll plaza. The owner must provide Aadhaar or any other required document while applying for the pass. The pass will be valid only at the toll plaza for which it has been issued. If a service road or alternative road is available for use by vehicle drivers, a concessional local pass will not be issued.

stories.title: Formalin tanker overturns in Lucknow, affects area within 5 km:One lane of Kisan Path remains closed after 15 hours
stories.summary: Fifteen hours after a tanker loaded with formalin overturned on Kisan Path in Lucknow's BKT area, efforts to dispose of the chemical are still under way. Soil is being spread on the road in an attempt to neutralise the chemical. As a safety measure, one side of the highway and the service lane have been closed. Police and ambulances are stationed at the site. The accident occurred at around 7:30 p.m. on Monday near the Manpur-Bana underpass. After the tanker overturned, people within a radius of around 2 kilometres experienced eye irritation and breathing difficulties. The effects of the chemical were felt up to around 5 kilometres away. See 3 pictures... Police deployed 500 metres ahead, traffic diverted BKТ police have deployed personnel around 500 metres from the scene. Traffic has been diverted on the Kisan Path from Raitha to Faizabad. Vehicle movement has been affected as one side of the highway and the service lane have been closed. See three pictures of the incident at night- Personnel reached the tanker wearing oxygen masks Following the report of the incident, police, fire brigade and SDRF teams had reached the spot. Medical teams had also been called in. Soil is now being spread on the road to dispose of the chemical. SDRF and police personnel are reaching the tanker wearing oxygen masks. Breathing difficulties and eye irritation are increasing when they approach the tanker. The personnel are therefore taking every precaution. Tanker was headed to a plywood factory The tanker was travelling from Sandila in Hardoi to a plywood factory in Gudamba. Police have called the factory employees to the spot to neutralise the effects of formalin. It was used to preserve bodies DG Health Pawan Kumar said that formalin is a chemical liquid. It is used to preserve bodies, preserve tissue for medical examinations, and make the glue used in plywood and furniture. Exposure to its vapours and strong odour can cause irritation to the eyes, nose, throat and skin, as well as breathing difficulties. Police said that people in the vicinity may experience irritation. Medical teams are present at the site. Those experiencing irritation have been advised to wash the affected area with clean water.

stories.title: Cyclonic storm to affect Gorakhpur:Rain likely with strong winds, temperature set to drop
stories.summary: The weather in Gorakhpur has gradually begun to change. There is a growing chill in the mornings and evenings, while strong sunshine during the day is making it feel warm. The sky has been clear since Tuesday morning, with bright sunshine. Temperatures have begun to fall, making the weather cooler in the mornings and at night. According to the Meteorological Department, the maximum temperature on Tuesday is expected to be 31°C, while the minimum temperature is likely to be 18°C. The weather in Gorakhpur may begin to change from Wednesday. According to meteorologists, the influence of a western disturbance could bring cloudy skies and rain. Fluctuations in the weather may be seen over the next three days. Rain is expected to bring down daytime and night-time temperatures. This could lead to increased cold in the mornings and evenings. However, it is important to keep an eye on the Meteorological Department's latest forecast to know when and how much rain is likely. Weather likely to change due to Cyclonic Storm 'Ornav' The cyclonic storm 'Ornaw', which has formed over the Bay of Bengal, is expected to affect the weather in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Under its influence, Gorakhpur and neighbouring districts may experience strong winds and rain. According to Gautam Gupta, district disaster expert with the District Disaster Management Authority, the storm is likely to affect eastern Uttar Pradesh on 29 and 30 October. Likely to make landfall on 28 October District disaster expert Gautam Gupta said the cyclonic storm is likely to make landfall on 28 October. Its impact may then be felt in eastern Uttar Pradesh on 29 and 30 October. Strong winds and rain are expected during this period. However, the actual impact of the storm in Gorakhpur and the intensity of the rain will depend on the weather conditions and the latest forecast issued by the department. Keep an eye on weather department updates People need to remain alert in view of the possible change in the weather. In the event of strong winds or rain, they should avoid standing near trees, electricity poles and weak structures. People should keep an eye on alerts issued by the Meteorological Department and the district administration. For now, bright sunshine is forecast during the day on Tuesday, while the cold may intensify in the morning and evening.

stories.title: Bodies of 3 businessmen found in car submerged in pond:Returning from Bahraich after visiting son, car pulled out using crane
stories.summary: Three businessmen's bodies were found in an Alto car submerged in a pond in Sitapur. Some villagers returning home from duty saw something floating in the pond. When they shone a torch, they saw the car's roof. They immediately informed the police. When the police had the car pulled out with the help of a crane, two bodies were found on the front seats and one on the rear seat. Documents found near the bodies identified them as Rakesh Chaurasia (50), Satish Nirmal (40) and Ramendra Singh (62). When the police spoke to the families, they learnt that Rakesh's son had been injured in an accident in Bahraich. Rakesh had left for Bahraich with two friends on Monday morning to see him. They spoke to their families while returning in the evening, after which there was no further contact. The incident took place in Panchpeer village under the Kamalapur police station area, 42 kilometres from the district headquarters. Station House Officer Atul Chaudhary said the bodies had been sent for post-mortem examinations. CCTV footage is being examined. All aspects related to the incident are being investigated. See two pictures of the accident- Here is the full case, explained step by step- According to reports, Mohan, the son of Sidhauli resident Rakesh Chaurasia, was injured in an accident in Bahraich on Sunday. He suffered minor injuries. Rakesh planned to go to Bahraich to bring him home. When Rakesh told his friends, Satish, a resident of Sidhauli, and Ramendra, a resident of Ateria, they also expressed a desire to accompany him. At 4 a.m. on Monday, the three travelled to Bahraich in Satish's Alto car (UP 32 EE 4038). In the evening, his son Mohan returned home with a friend. He said that his father and his friends had stayed back in Bahraich for some work and would leave later. However, when the three had not returned home by night, the family became worried. The family members began calling them, but none of the phones could be reached. They then lodged a complaint with the police. On Tuesday, the family searched for them with the police throughout the day, but no trace of them was found. At around 1.30 a.m., residents of Panchpeer village informed the police that a car had fallen into the village pond. The police had the car pulled out and found bodies inside. In its initial investigation, the police suspected that the victims had died by drowning.

stories.title: Mangalpur villagers in Varanasi suffer from fever:Falling platelets and liver swelling reported; health department blames water problems
stories.summary: Fever has been spreading in Mangalpur village for around one and a half to two months. Villagers claim that four people have died in the village. More than one member of several families is ill. Patients are reporting high fever, pain in the body and joints, vomiting, nausea, weakness and low platelet counts. They are also experiencing swelling of the liver. Villagers said there is a pond in the village into which the entire village's wastewater flows, and that the illness began there. Water does flow into the pond, but there is no drainage system. District Malaria Officer Sharad Chandra Pandey, who visited the village for an inspection, said 58 people had so far been tested in three phases. None of them tested positive for malaria or dengue, while four cases of typhoid were detected. During the preliminary inspection, the officer suspected a water-related problem. Regarding the four deaths reported by the villagers, the officer said they had occurred for different reasons. Complaints of liver swelling along with fever Village doctor Pravesh Mishra said that more than 30 patients with similar symptoms had come to him over the past month. The patients are showing symptoms resembling a viral infection. Some patients are testing positive for typhoid. They are complaining of high fever, vomiting, nausea, body aches and weakness. They are also suffering from low platelet counts and liver swelling. According to the doctor, some patients have been found to have significantly elevated liver test levels. He said that while the level is normally around 40, it has risen to between 400 and 900 in some patients. The doctor said that several members of the same household are falling ill in the village. According to him, patients are developing further complications after the fever. Patients in every household, claim that four people have died Ansari, a resident of the village, said the illness had been spreading there for around two months. They said people were developing fevers and complaining of low platelet counts. According to them, four people had also died in the surrounding area. Another villager, Parvez Alam, said the illness sp widely from the Pokhari locality in Mangalpur and gradually began affecting people in the other neighbourhoods of the village as well. He said several members of some families had fallen ill, while some had to be admitted to hospital. Villagers say the illness has caused fear among people in the village. They are unable to determine whether the problem is being caused by a viral infection, contaminated water or some other reason. Grandmother admitted to hospital with grandson Jadawati Devi, who has been admitted to hospital with her grandson, said he had been ill for around ten days. His platelet count is low and he has also been suffering from swelling in the liver. The children continue to experience lethargy and weakness. Jadawati Devi said several people in the village were ill. They could not understand what was causing the illness to spread. Villagers suspect that the problem of filth and contaminated water in the village could be the cause. Platelet count was 12,000 A resident of Mangalpur said that his 55-year-old sister, Zulekha Bano, died on 2 October. According to him, Zulekha was admitted to Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital on 1 October after her condition deteriorated. The family said doctors informed them that her platelet count was 12,000 and that she had swelling in her liver. She was also suffering from fever and abdominal pain. According to the family, Zulekha Bano died at around 10:50 pm on 2 October. The family said several other people in the village were also ill, and some had to be admitted to hospital. Villagers have claimed that four people have died in the village. However, the District Malaria Officer said the deaths were caused by different reasons. A 70-year-old man died of a brain tumour. A 55-year-old woman had been suffering from typhoid and septicaemia for a long time. One person had a mental health problem. Water turning yellow, demand for pond cleaning and drainage Villagers say that water drawn from the submersible pump turns yellow after being kept in a bucket for some time. Some villagers also complained that the water smells bad. According to the villagers, water from the surrounding area collects in the village pond. Several attempts have been made to drain it, but the problem has not been permanently resolved. They say the pond needs to be drained and cleaned. A villager said that a permanent solution could be found by creating an arrangement to drain the pond towards the ring road. The villagers are demanding that the pond be cleaned and that arrangements be made to provide clean drinking water. Selling jewellery to pay for treatment, and even daily-wage work has stopped The financial condition of residents in Manglapur village is also deteriorating because of the illness. Residents said that with several people in their households falling ill, it had become difficult to bear the cost of treatment. Some families have even had to sell their savings and jewellery to pay for treatment. One resident said that his son used to work as a daily wage labourer, but the illness had affected the family's income. According to the residents, they have already spent between ₹25,000 and ₹40,000 on the treatment of some patients. In such a situation, families are finding it difficult to arrange daily expenses and food while also paying for treatment. DMO says 58 people tested, no dengue or malaria cases found District Malaria Officer Sharad Chandra Pandey said officials had tested 58 people in Manglapur in three phases so far. The tests did not detect a single case of dengue or malaria, while four cases of typhoid were found. The officer also said that no dengue larvae had been found in the village.

stories.title: Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers’ constituency observer removed:Relieved of duty following BJP MLC’s complaint; Prakash Bindu given charge
stories.summary: The chief electoral officer relieved 2007-batch IAS officer Abhay Singh of his responsibility as observer for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Division Teachers' Constituency a day before counting began, following a complaint by BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh. In his place, 2009-batch IAS officer Prakash Bindu has been given the responsibility. He was asked to report to the constituency immediately. He reached Gorakhpur on Monday evening. Devendra Singh emailed the Election Commission of India, citing a CBI FIR against Abhay Singh. He later wrote an open letter to the counting personnel. The move is believed to have been taken to avoid any kind of controversy. Complaint filed on polling day itself On polling day during the teachers' MLC election, 23 October at 10:36 a.m., MLC Devendra Singh emailed the Election Commission of India, demanding the removal of the observer appointed here, Abhay Singh. He had questioned the officer's appointment. The MLC had said that the CBI had registered a case against the officer in 2019 in connection with illegal mining. A large amount of cash was recovered during the raid at his residence. The MLC had demanded that the current status of the CBI investigation and the facts related to it be taken serious cognisance of. He had said that a fair election could not be expected from such a tainted officer. Taking cognisance of the MLC's complaint, the Election Commission removed the observer a day before the counting of votes. A new officer has been given the responsibility in his place. The Samajwadi Party candidate's camp is also pleased after the observer's removal. Samajwadi Party candidate Dr Sanjayan said, "It is appropriate that such an observer has been removed. This is the first success." Know what the BJP MLC said BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh welcomed the Election Commission's decision. "The corrupt and dishonest officer has been removed. I thank the Election Commission of India for this. The state's most corrupt officer has been removed and an honest officer with a clean image has been appointed as the observer."

stories.title: Shraddha allegedly forced model to spend night with officer:Kept her locked in room for 7 days and beat her after she refused
stories.summary: Lucknow businessman Shiva Sharma died 21 days ago. Model Shraddha Dubey has been in jail for the last 8 days on charges of murder. Police are reaching out to people associated with Shraddha. It has come to light that Shraddha was pressuring a girl to spend a night with a senior official. After the girl refused, Shraddha subjected her to an ordeal that still makes the girl shudder just thinking about it. Shraddha kept the girl confined in her flat for seven days. She continued to threaten her after beating her up. When the girl did not back down, Shraddha let her go. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the girl and her friend. Read the full story step-by-step… This story begins in the winter of January 2026. Shraddha Dubey and her friends were present at a late-night party at a club in Gomti Nagar. Dancing was underway, and drinks were flowing. There was a girl at this party who was playing music. Shraddha's eyes fell upon her, and Shraddha took a liking to her at first sight. After the party, Shraddha met the girl. It turned out that she also did modelling. Following this, Shraddha started talking to the girl on WhatsApp. The girl lived in a flat in an apartment located in Papermill Colony, and after four–five meetings, she developed a good friendship with Shraddha. Shraddha often used to boast about her clout in bureaucracy and her power. The girl told Dainik Bhaskar—"Shraddha had a bit of influence in Lucknow's modeling events. I was in need of work. Everything was going normally. The real story began in August 2026." hosted, "One night, Shraddha suddenly made a WhatsApp call and called me to meet her at her flat. I thought there was an event to be hosted and we needed to discuss it. When I arrived, it was around 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM. Shraddha and a friend of hers were present. After I arrived, Shraddha asked her friend to step outside. Then she told me, 'How long will you keep hosting parties like this? If you want to become rich, learn to make a few compromises…' She then said to me, 'You just have to stay with an officer for one night and do whatever he says.' “I was shocked hearing all this. I couldn't understand what to say. Then I refused Shraddha. That night, I returned home.” “The dark persona behind Shraddha's beautiful face was gradually coming to light. After three-four days, Shraddha called me to her flat again. First, she threatened me, saying that I would have to obey her no matter what, otherwise it would become difficult for me to live in Lucknow. But I clearly refused her. I could not do all this for a bit of money or a career…” "After this, Shraddha beat me up and stripped off my clothes. She locked me inside a room. There was a blanket there, which I kept wrapped around myself for 7 days. When Shraddha realised that I would not bow down before her, she let me go, but threatened that if I opened my mouth anywhere, she would have me 'disappeared'. I was terrified, so I never filed a complaint anywhere." The official had said— "Handle this yourself…" The girl said— "When Shraddha was threatening me, she was also revealing her bureaucratic links. From what she was saying, I felt that perhaps she had asked an official to teach me a lesson, but he did not want to get involved in this matter. Therefore, he told Shraddha, 'You handle this yourself.' Only after that did Shraddha call me over and commit atrocities against me." When I told my family about Shraddha's connections, they also quieted down Dainik Bhaskar team asked— Does your family know about this? Was there no pressure to lodge a complaint? The girl said— “When I didn't reach home, my roommate informed my family. However, since I used to go out of town to host events as well, no one went to the police immediately.” "After my return, I had to tell my family about my ordeal. They were angry and wanted to go to the police. But during my stay at Shraddha's flat, I had also seen her connections. Calls from influential people used to come on her mobile. Therefore, I thought it best to remain silent and explained the same to my family. That is why no major fuss was made."

stories.title: SP gets 3,123 more votes than BJP in MLC polls:Graduate voters back Akhilesh; teachers support BJP
stories.summary: In the Uttar Pradesh MLC elections, the BJP won six seats, and the Samajwadi Party won five. The BJP won four of the six teachers' constituency seats, while the SP won two. In the graduates' constituency, the SP won three of the five seats, and the BJP won two. Although the BJP won more seats than the SP, the SP led in vote share. The SP received 3,123 more votes than the BJP, a difference of around 0.45%. There were 1,481,310 voters in the election. Of these, 1,185,706 were registered for the five graduates' constituency seats, while 295,604 were registered for the six teachers' constituency seats. A total of 55.54% of voters, or 658,542 people, voted on 23 October. The BJP received a total of 86,120 votes across the six teachers' constituency seats and 1,75,259 votes across the five graduates' constituency seats. In total, the BJP received 2,61,379 votes. The SP, meanwhile, received 2,12,116 votes across the five graduates' constituency seats and 52,386 votes across the five teachers' constituency seats. Thus, the SP received a total of 264,502 votes. 'Educated' class with SP, teachers with BJP The election results for the teachers' and graduates' seats in the Legislative Council have revealed an interesting trend. The state's teachers appear to be with the BJP, while graduates' voters appear to support the Samajwadi Party. The SP won the Lucknow and Allahabad-Jhansi graduates' seats. Meanwhile, SP candidate Ashutosh Sinha won the Varanasi teachers' constituency seat. The BJP won the Meerut and Agra graduates' seats. In the teachers' constituencies, the BJP won the Lucknow, Bareilly-Moradabad, Faizabad-Gorakhpur and Meerut seats. The SP won the Agra and Varanasi constituency seats among teachers.

stories.title: BSc student killed by thresher, limbs missing:Family gathers remains in sheet after intestines spill out in Farrukhabad
stories.summary: A 23-year-old BSc student died after getting trapped in a thresher while threshing millet in Farrukhabad, Uttar Pradesh, on Thursday evening. The accident happened at around 6 pm in the Nawabganj police station area. The machine severed one of his hands and a leg, which could not be found after the accident. The student, Anubhav, suffered severe injuries in the accident. People present at the spot managed to open the machine and take his body out. They wrapped the body in a sheet and informed the police. Police later sent it for a post-mortem examination. Student went to the field to thresh millet Anubhav was the only son of Tirumal Singh, 59, who lives with his family in Beg village, around 20 km from the district headquarters. His mother, Anita Devi, is 50 years old. The family also includes his three sisters, Kanchan, Ritu, 24, and Gargi, 17. Kanchan is married, while Ritu and Gargi live at home. Anubhav was studying in the third year of a BSc degree. His father has a disability in one leg. At around 5:30 pm on Thursday, Anubhav went to his field to thresh millet. After finishing the work, he began threshing millet for Pushpendra, who lives in the same village. Pushpendra, his brother Sanjeev and tractor driver Lalla were also present. Body taken out of the machine During the work, Anubhav's hand got caught in the thresher, and his body was pulled into the machine. The accident left him with fatal injuries. The people present at the spot managed to open the machine and remove his body. His injuries were severe, and his hand and leg could not be found. Police reached the spot after receiving information about the accident and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Police investigating the incident Station House Officer Rajeev Kumar said a police team reached the spot after receiving information about the accident. He said the matter was being investigated and further action would be taken based on the findings.

stories.title: Rebellion in Kanpur BJP as regional chief defies state president:IT cell convenor, co-convenor replaced
stories.summary: The BJP's regional president in Kanpur has revolted against the party leadership. Ramkishore Sahu has refused to accept the IT Cell office-bearers announced by the state leadership. Setting aside the names finalised by the party leadership in Lucknow, he has appointed a new convener and co-convener on his own. He sent a letter regarding the appointments to the party's state office on 24 October, which came to light today (Thursday). This is the first time a BJP regional president has challenged a decision taken by the state headquarters. Speaking on the matter, Ramkishore Sahu said, "I have formed a new IT Cell team. I have appointed Mayank Bhatt as the convener and Surendra Vishwakarma as the co-convener. Surendra Vishwakarma lives in Jhansi." "The IT Cell handles day-to-day work, so we needed a worker from Kanpur itself. That is why I appointed Mayank Bhatt as the convener. The team will be expanded further," he said. Understand the entire controversy in 5 points 1. On 22 October, under the leadership of state president Pankaj Chaudhary, a new team of IT Cell office-bearers was announced for six organisational regions: Awadh, West, Braj, Kanpur-Bundelkhand, Kashi and Gorakhpur. 2. Under the announcement, Surendra Vishwakarma was appointed IT Cell convener for the Kanpur region, while Abhishek Pandey was named co-convener. 3. As soon as the list was released, Kanpur regional president Ramkishore Sahu raised objections. He said the names had been finalised by ignoring the recommendations he had submitted. 4. It was not just Kanpur. Vinod Rai, the regional president in Gorakhpur, had also expressed dissatisfaction over appointments to the IT and social media cells in his region. 5. Amid the standoff with the state leadership, Ramkishore Sahu took a firm step and rejected the list issued by Lucknow. He removed Surendra Vishwakarma as convener and appointed Mayank Bhatt in his place. Surendra was demoted to the position of co-convener, while Abhishek Pandey was removed from the team altogether. This has happened for the first time in the history of the UP BJP This is being considered the first instance in the history of the Uttar Pradesh BJP in which a regional president has directly disregarded an order issued by the state president. All eyes are now on what action the state headquarters will take over this open act of indiscipline.

stories.title: VIDEO | Lucknow triple murder:Accused opens fire as family members scream and plead for help
stories.summary: Live video of the Lucknow triple murder has emerged. It shows the accused, Rishabh, firing repeatedly at all three victims. During the incident, family members kept screaming, but the accused continued firing fearlessly. In the video, Rishabh first shot Shambhu, then Shiva Tiwari and subsequently his son Suyash. The broad-daylight incident spread panic throughout the area. A second video showing the police apprehending the accused has also emerged on social media. Police had arrested him at the scene itself. The area has remained tense since the triple murder. Police arrested the accused, Rishabh Shukla, immediately after the incident. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak had assured that action would be taken against the accused under the NSA. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak had met the family members After the post-mortem, people blocked the road as the bodies of the father, son and brother reached home. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak and BJP state vice-president Neeraj Singh also reached the deceased's home. As soon as people saw them, they raised slogans such as "Bulldozer rule has gone to sleep". However, the Deputy CM quietly folded his hands and went inside to meet the family. After this, the Deputy CM announced that Ruchi Tiwari, the wife of Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, would be given a government job. The daughter's education would be free for life. The family would be provided security. Action would be taken against the accused under the National Security Act (NSA). Deputy CM also shouldered the bier After the Deputy CM's assurance, the family members agreed to take all three bodies for the last rites. The Deputy CM also shouldered the bier and placed wood on the pyre. The last rites of all three bodies were performed at Gulala Ghat around 5 hours after the post-mortem. Accused's house boundary wall demolished within 6 hours About six hours after the Deputy Chief Minister's assurance, the boundary wall of accused Rishabh Shukla's house was demolished by a Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) bulldozer at 10 p.m. The LDA officials had sealed the house earlier in the evening. Belongings were removed from the homes of other family members, including the accused's uncle Girish. Meanwhile, Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba had suspended Saadatganj police station Inspector Santosh Kumar Arya and outpost in-charge Ajay Kumar Chaurasia on Tuesday. 3 people were killed in a dispute over car parking and a raised platform On Monday morning, Rishabh Shukla (30) shot dead three people in Brahman Tola, Saadatganj, over a dispute concerning car parking and a raised platform. The deceased, Shivaji Tiwari (62), was a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the RSS district general secretary. Shivaji's brother, Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Shivaji's son Suyash (30) ran an electrical goods business. He was due to get married on 5 December. The accused, Rishabh, was a navigation officer in the Merchant Navy.

stories.title: Fatwa issued against actress Sara Ali Khan in UP:Cleric says Muslims visiting Kedarnath is forbidden, urges her to seek Allah’s forgiveness
stories.summary: A fatwa has been issued against Bollywood actress Sara Ali Khan. Bareilly-based cleric Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi said that, according to Islam and Sharia, it is unlawful and forbidden for a Muslim to worship at a temple. He said she should seek forgiveness from Allah. Sara visited Kedarnath Dham on 25 October, where she offered prayers and performed rituals. In 2017, she spent around two months there while shooting for her film Kedarnath. She has now offered prayers at the Kedarnath and Lord Tungnath temples around five times. Read the Maulana’s full statement below… Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi, national president of the All India Muslim Jamaat, expressed his religious views on actress Sara Ali Khan offering prayers at Kedarnath temple. He said several Muslim youths had asked him whether Islamic Sharia permitted such practices. He was responding to their questions. The Maulana said, “I want to make it clear that Islamic Sharia does not permit its followers to engage in shirk. This means that no Muslim, whether a man or a woman, is allowed to adopt the religious practices of another faith or worship at a temple.” He said Sara Ali Khan is a well-known Indian actress. She visited Kedarnath temple, offered prayers and stood in the queue for around half an hour. According to the Maulana, her actions are unlawful and forbidden under Sharia. He also described her as an offender and sinner from the perspective of Sharia. The Maulana said Sara Ali Khan should repent and seek forgiveness from God. According to him, if she does not do so, she would be guilty of a major sin under Sharia. Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi clarified that these were his personal religious views and statements. They should not be regarded as the unanimous opinion of all Muslim clerics or the entire Islamic community. See pictures… Sara spent three days in Kedarnath, says, ‘Baba’s shrine is my home’ Sara Ali Khan stayed in Uttarakhand from 25 to 27 October. She reached the shrine by helicopter. She was seen wearing simple clothes and a cap, which meant many people did not recognise her. Those who recognised Sara also took photographs with her. From the first day, she attended the morning and evening aarti before going out to explore the surrounding areas with friends. Sara met local residents and asked them about their lives. During her visit, she made six to seven new friends in the Kedarnath valley and asked them about nearby trekking destinations. It also snowed in Kedarnath after Sara arrived. She was seen wearing warm clothes because of the cold. On Tuesday evening, she took a helicopter to Dehradun before leaving for Mumbai. Sara says, ‘Kedarnath is my home; I have felt connected to it since 2017’ Sara told Ankit Bajpai, who has been staying in Kedarnath for several months, that Kedarnath felt like home to her. “Since 2017, I have tried to visit the shrine every year to seek Baba’s blessings,” she said. She also made several reels with Ankit Bajpai. Sara took photographs of Kedarnath Dham on her phone, which she plans to share later. At night, she also sat down for tea with local people. The actress may also visit the Third Kedar, Shri Tungnath temple. Last year, on 22 October, Sara visited Kedarnath and Tungnath and shared photographs on social media. Sara stood in the queue for half an hour to seek Baba’s blessings On Sunday, 25 October, Sara stood in the queue for around half an hour. People present at the shrine did not recognise her. Seeing her shivering in the cold, some women standing nearby offered her a shawl, but they did not realise who she was. Sara had arrived at the shrine with her friends. She also visited Baba Bhukunt Bhairav, regarded as the protector of Kedarnath. The Shri Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC) had earlier said that it would restrict the entry of non-Sanatanis into the temples. The committee had stated that Sara Ali Khan would first have to submit an affidavit declaring her faith in Sanatan Dharma before being allowed to enter Kedarnath. As the controversy grew, BKTC chairman Hemant Dwivedi said that everyone who believes in Sanatan Dharma is welcome. Sara visits Kedarnath before Diwali Sara’s first spiritual and professional connection with Kedarnath dates back to 2017, when she shot her debut film Kedarnath there. She has continued to visit the shrine since then. In October 2024, just before Diwali, she offered prayers at Kedarnath temple and shared photographs. In 2023, she visited the shrine twice. She visited Kedarnath and Tungnath on 6 May 2023 and returned to Kedarnath around six months later, in October. In November 2021, Sara Ali Khan also visited Kedarnath with her friend and fellow actress Janhvi Kapoor. Sara Ali Khan visited Kashi Vishwanath six years ago In 2020, Sara Ali Khan visited Shri Kashi Vishwanath temple in Varanasi and offered prayers. At the time, she was shooting for a film in the city with her mother, Amrita Singh. Two days earlier, she had attended the Ganga aarti. She then performed Shodashopachara puja at Kashi Vishwanath temple and touched the Shivling. Saints and scholars had objected to this at the time. Photographs from 22 October 2025 She worshipped at Mahakaleshwar three years ago In 2022, Sara Ali Khan attended the Bhasma Aarti dedicated to Lord Mahakal at the Mahakaleshwar temple in Ujjain. After the ritual, she entered the sanctum to seek the deity’s blessings and sat in Nandi Hall, chanting mantras for around half an hour.

stories.title: Schools up to Class 12 shut in 60 UP districts:PET exam expected to draw heavy crowds, says DIOS
stories.summary: Schools up to Class 12 will remain closed in 60 Uttar Pradesh districts on 30 October due to the PET examination. District Inspectors of Schools (DIOS) have issued orders in this regard. According to the Lucknow DIOS, the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission’s PET 2026 examination will be held in two shifts on 30 October and 1 November at 45 centres. Around 20,000–25,000 candidates, along with their parents, are expected to arrive for each shift, potentially leading to heavy crowds in the city. The DIOS said a one-day academic holiday had been declared for schools on 30 October following approval from the competent authority. Officials have been directed to ensure strict compliance with the order. Story being updated...

stories.title: Bhaskar sting triggers raids at 40 UP blood banks:7 licences suspended; untested blood sold to patients
stories.summary: Students in Uttar Pradesh are being forced to sell their blood to cover the cost of their education. A major nexus is operating behind this. The Daily Bhaskar sting operation has had a significant impact. Within 48 hours of the report being published, raids began at blood banks across Uttar Pradesh. Investigations are under way from Prayagraj to Lucknow. Action has been taken against three blood banks in Lucknow and one each in Agra, Aligarh, Gorakhpur and Lakhimpur Kheri. Blood was being given to patients here without testing, which could pose a risk of serious infections. In addition, several irregularities were found, including negligence in maintaining the cold chain and a shortage of technical staff. The Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) has also raided 40 charitable blood banks, of which the licences of seven have been suspended with immediate effect. On 26 October, an exclusive investigation was published on the Dainik Bhaskar app. Its headline was: 'Students are selling their blood to pay for their studies; NEET aspirant in Uttar Pradesh says, "The blood will keep being produced, but I may never get another chance to study."' In the report, we exposed a gang and nexus that was exploiting their circumstances to draw blood multiple times in a single month from young students, particularly those preparing for competitive examinations. As soon as the news emerged, an uproar erupted on social media and in political circles. Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav, Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav, YouTuber Neha Singh Rathore and several leaders and organisations, including the National Congress, cited Bhaskar's report and held the system accountable. The administration swung into action as pressure mounted from all sides. Simultaneous raids in 10 districts on FSDA commissioner’s orders Following the impact of the report, a special inter-district team of drug inspectors was formed on the direct orders of Dr Roshan Jacob, Commissioner of the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA). The team simultaneously raided 40 blood banks run by charitable trusts and societies across 10 major districts of Uttar Pradesh. Blood was distributed without testing, putting patients’ lives at risk The shortcomings and shocking facts uncovered during the raids were enough to send a chill down anyone’s spine. Several blood banks were found supplying blood directly to patients without conducting the mandatory tests. Under the rules, to ensure patient safety, donated blood must be tested for dangerous diseases such as HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, syphilis and malaria. It is also essential to store blood at a specified temperature. However, the raids revealed that testing machines were not working at several locations, while proper cold-chain facilities were nowhere to be found. Operations of these seven blood banks halted immediately After serious irregularities and life-threatening negligence were detected, the FSDA has suspended the operations of seven major blood banks with immediate effect. 1. Little Star Blood Centre, Lucknow: The doctor in charge and the technical staff had been found absent for a long time. The most shocking finding was that the ELISA testing machine was non-functional, yet blood and its components were being sold without testing. Fragments of red blood cells were found in the fresh frozen plasma, which is extremely dangerous. 2. Rama Charitable Blood Centre, Lucknow: Blood was being issued without ELISA testing. FFP had been improperly stored in a platelet agitator. In addition, patients' relatives were being charged more than the rates fixed by the government. 3. KHS Charitable Blood Centre, Lucknow: Neither a doctor nor any technical staff member was present at the site. There was no trace of the master register or ELISA/TTI testing. Moreover, the entire centre was extremely dirty. 4. Shri Balaji Charitable Blood Centre, Agra: Neither the mandatory ELISA test nor sterility testing was being carried out here. The names, addresses, mobile numbers and even signatures of blood donors were not recorded. The temperature stock record was also completely missing. 5. New Bapu Blood Centre, Aligarh: Serious irregularities were found in infection screening (TTI) and the CPDA solution. The ELISA test was not being conducted here either. There was no trace of qualified staff or the required documents. 6. Maanya Charitable Blood Centre, Gorakhpur: When the inspection team arrived, neither the doctor in charge nor any technical staff was present. Record-keeping was found to be completely incomplete. 7. Anubhav Charitable Blood Centre, Lakhimpur Kheri: It did not even have registration for the disposal of biomedical waste (hazardous waste). The temperature-monitoring and alarm systems were completely non-functional. Advisory sent to all DMs FSDA Commissioner Dr Roshan Jacob has made it clear that the blood and blood components stored at the seven blood banks where operations have been halted will be safely disposed of. A strict advisory has been issued to all the concerned district magistrates to ensure that the unsafe blood does not reach the market or any patient. Show-cause notices are being served to the remaining blood banks where minor deficiencies have been found. The government has made it clear that there will be no compromise on patients' health or the quality of blood in the state. Dainik Bhaskar will continue to raise such issues fearlessly.

stories.title: Azam Khan’s 10-year sentence suspended:Son also gets relief as High Court rules in double PAN card case
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam have received relief in the double PAN card case. The Allahabad High Court has suspended their 10-year prison sentence and granted them bail. However, the court has refused to stay their conviction. Both had challenged the trial court’s verdict, seeking a stay on their conviction, suspension of their sentence and release on interim bail. After hearing the case on October 15, a single-judge bench of Justice Samit Gopal had reserved its verdict. Following the High Court’s order, former MLA Abdullah Azam may be released from jail, but Azam Khan’s release is still uncertain. According to senior Supreme Court advocate Shariq Abbasi, two other cases against Azam Khan are pending, in which the police have not yet obtained warrants. One case is related to the Enforcement Directorate (ED), while the other concerns the Vigilance Department. Both agencies have registered cases in recent days. It is believed that Azam Khan could also be released from jail if no B-warrants are issued in these cases. This news is being updated

stories.title: No UP govt jobs for violent regime-change links:New rules cover murder, rape and paper leaks; FIR alone won't disqualify
stories.summary: Young people who take to the streets and engage in violence to bring about a regime change in Uttar Pradesh will not be eligible for government jobs. The state government has amended the rules governing character certificates for candidates selected through direct recruitment in its various departments, councils, corporations and local bodies. Gen-Z protests were held in Delhi, Lucknow and several states across the country, including Uttar Pradesh. Protests were also held against Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar. Some organisations had also called for a regime change during the protests. The BJP has accused the Opposition of trying to change the government through violence in connection with these demonstrations. M. Devaraj, Additional Chief Secretary of the Appointment and Personnel Department, issued the new rules following an order of the High Court. Under the rules, a person will be considered ineligible for a government job if they are a member of an organisation whose objective is to change the system through violence. However, no one will be disqualified on the basis of their political ideology. Under the new rules, a candidate will not be eligible for a government job if they are found to be an accused or convicted in cases related to murder, robbery, rape, outraging a woman's modesty, corruption, terrorist activities, paper leaks or solver gangs. Filing of an FIR at the age of 21 could put government job at risk If such a case is registered against a person after they turn 21, and they are found to have been involved in any activity linked to changing the government within three years of the date of the investigation, this will be considered an indication that they are still active in such activities. However, if positive changes are seen in their views and behaviour during this period, their appointment to a government job may be considered. Filing of an FIR will not lead to disqualification from a job The new rules make it clear that a candidate will not be considered ineligible for a government job merely because an FIR has been registered or an investigation is under way. The candidate will also not be automatically disqualified in cases resulting in acquittal, settlement, or those covered under the Juvenile Justice law. Employees already working in government jobs will not undergo character verification again. Even if the character verification process has not been completed, the candidate will not be stopped from receiving an appointment letter. For this, the candidate will be required to submit a self-declaration and fill in the prescribed form, after which a provisional appointment letter will be issued. If the candidate provides incorrect information or is found ineligible during character verification, the appointment will be cancelled immediately. Legal action will also be taken against the candidate. Report to be submitted within 30 days The district police or the local intelligence unit (LIU) will have to submit its report to the appointing authority within 30 days of receiving the verification application. The Home Department will monitor the entire process.

stories.title: ₹5 crore cash found in blue drums in Prayagraj:3 blue drums stuffed with ₹500 notes; police cut village power before raid
stories.summary: More than ₹5 crore in cash has been found in three drums buried underground in Prayagraj. The drums were filled with bundles of ₹500 notes. Police have detained four people. An Income Tax Department team will count the notes today, Thursday. The case relates to Baraipur Ramnagar village in Nawabganj. How the police got a tip-off and dug up the drums According to the police, they received information late on Wednesday evening that money stolen from the house of Baraipur Ramnagar resident Rakesh Yadav, alias Mahakal, had been buried underground. As soon as they received the information, a police team, including DCP Gangnagar Sonam Kumar and ADCP Gangnagar Pushkar Verma, reached the spot. Before this, the police had the electricity supply to the entire village cut off. They then launched a search operation. During a search of the house, three drums buried underground were found. They were filled with bundles of notes. The police seized the cash and sealed it. Police cut off village’s electricity before conducting raid Rakesh Yadav, alias Mahakal, has his ancestral house in Bareipur village in the Nawabganj area. Police received a tip-off that he had buried stolen money inside his house. The information reached Police Commissioner Piyush Mordia. On Wednesday at 6 pm, a police team led by DCP (Ganganagar) Sonam Kumar and ADCP Pushkar Verma reached the spot. Before the raid, the police cut off the electricity supply to the entire village and then launched a search operation. ACP (Soraon) Shyamjeet Pramila Singh was also present. Search operation lasted four and a half hours According to the police, three blue drums buried in the ground were found during the search of the house. Bundles of cash wrapped in cloth had been kept inside them. The police seized the cash, sealed the house and cordoned off the area. After searching the house for around four and a half hours, the police left at 10.30 pm. They also detained Rakesh Yadav’s brother, Bablu. Police teams took the entire family with them. More than 40 police personnel have been deployed around the house. The police have also cordoned off Rakesh’s garden and vacant land, along with the house, using security tape. Villagers claim he bought 22 bighas of land within a few years Villagers said Rakesh Yadav had lived in Pune several years ago with his brother-in-law and his wife’s brother, working at a jewellery trader’s house. During the Covid pandemic, he returned to his home in Bareipur. After that, he bought 22 bighas of land worth more than ₹10 crore. He then spent around ₹1 crore building a house. He also bought two tractors, a DJ system and a pickup vehicle, before starting a cement and steel rod business in the village. Five to six days ago, Rakesh had a dispute with some neighbours, following which an FIR was registered against him. A sub-inspector visited the village to investigate the case, and an argument broke out between him and Rakesh Yadav. The police then began an investigation, which led to the discovery of claims that crores of rupees were hidden inside the house. Rakesh lives in the village with two of his brothers Rakesh has five brothers, making six brothers in total. Rakesh, Rajesh and Lavkush live in the village, while the other three—Chhotu, Rajendra and Abhishek—live elsewhere. Their father, Ram Aadhar, has died. DCP Ganganagar Sonam Kumar said: “Search operations were stopped on Wednesday night due to darkness. Police have been deployed around Rakesh’s house. Crores of rupees were recovered from three drums buried underground.”

stories.title: Did SP’s core voters not back Sanjayan?:Rajeev Yadav may have benefited from anger over ‘Yadav’ ticket denial
stories.summary: The result of the teachers' MLC election is out. Dr Sanjayan Tripathi, who was considered to be in a direct contest, was forced to finish third. The same Sanjayan had twice finished as runner-up in the graduates' constituency election from this region, and at that time he did not have the backing of any political party. This has sparked a debate: did he fail to receive the support of the Samajwadi Party's core voters? The Yadav community, considered the party's core voter base, is denying this. However, there is discussion behind the scenes that people were angry over Kamlesh Yadav being denied a ticket. The result of that was visible in the election. This resentment is also believed to have made an important contribution to Rajiv Yadav's strong contest. Akhilesh's Brahmin card, played by fielding Dr Sanjayan in the election, was not entirely successful. The party was forced into third place after failing to receive support from its own core voters. Akhilesh Yadav had initially nominated Kamlesh Yadav from the Gorakhpur-Faizabad divisional teachers' constituency. He changed the ticket just a day before Kamlesh Yadav was to file his nomination. However, Kamlesh Yadav was placated over the decision. The very next day, he was appointed national secretary. But there was resentment among Yadav leaders over the issue behind the scenes. In Azamgarh and Mau, where the Samajwadi Party appears to have a strong support base, Sanjayan received very few votes. Rajiv Yadav appeared to be quite strong there. Assembly elections likely to be affected Reports suggest that Yadav leaders are likely to be given very few tickets in the Assembly elections this time. There is still silence on the issue, but Yadav leaders are preparing in almost every Assembly constituency. In such a situation, doubts have now emerged over whether they will be able to accept someone else as the candidate. A debate has erupted on social media over Yadav voters not supporting Sanjayan, with influencers from the community clarifying that this is not the case. Political analysts say Akhilesh will have to devise a strategy on the issue, as he may have to deal with the resentment of Yadav leaders whose tickets are denied. What advantage will leaders from other castes gain? Following the results of the teachers' MLC election, there is also discussion over whether leaders from other castes will benefit from joining the SP. Given the ambitions at the local level, the development is a warning bell for newly joined Brahmin and Kshatriya leaders in the party. Doubts have emerged over whether they will receive the support of the core voters on whose strength they are joining the party in the election. Senior journalist Alok Dubey says there has been a reaction to Kamlesh Yadav being suddenly denied a ticket. The narrative that Yadavs are not being given tickets in the Assembly election could also hurt the Samajwadi Party. This, too, will have to be taken into account while distributing tickets.

stories.title: Mother, son die as Scorpio falls 30 feet in UP:Varanasi-bound SUV flips repeatedly, wheels detach; 3 injured
stories.summary: A Scorpio plunged 30 feet from an expressway in Ghazipur, killing a mother and her son who were travelling in it. Three people were seriously injured. People nearby saw the incident and informed the police. Police reached the spot, broke open the Scorpio's doors and pulled out those trapped inside. The injured were sent to hospital, where they were referred to the BHU Trauma Centre after receiving first aid. The police have placed the bodies in the mortuary. According to the preliminary investigation, the Scorpio was travelling at a speed of around 80-100. The vehicle broke through the iron grille installed on the expressway, overturned several times and fell 30 feet below. It came to a stop after hitting a pole. All the vehicle's airbags deployed. Its bonnet was badly damaged, and both rear wheels came off. The incident took place at pillar number 340 of the Greenfield Expressway, near Sheikhpur in the Jangipur police station area, 10 km from the headquarters. Here is the full sequence of events According to the police, Ballia resident Jayaram Upadhyay (58) was travelling from Ballia to Varanasi with his wife, Kshama (55), son Anmol (28) and three others. They included Ballia resident Manoj Chaubey (42), Mirzapur resident Ramesh Verma (32) and Varanasi resident Ratnesh Mishra (40). Ramesh Verma was driving the Scorpio. Scorpio falls 30 feet from expressway at 1 a.m. According to ASP Dr Rakesh Kumar Mishra, six people were travelling in the Scorpio. At around 1 a.m., the vehicle went out of control near pillar number 340 of the Greenfield Expressway in Sheikhpur, in the Jangipur police station area, broke through the railing and fell below. Kshama and her son Anmol died in the accident, while Manoj Chaubey, Ramesh Verma and Ratnesh Mishra were seriously injured. It is not clear whether Jayaram Upadhyay was also injured in the accident. Bonnet and boot severely damaged According to eyewitnesses, the accident occurred late at night. After hearing a sudden loud noise, villagers came out of their homes and saw a Scorpio breaking through the iron railing of the expressway and falling below. After hitting the railing, the vehicle fell down, somersaulting several times. The vehicle's front bonnet and rear boot were badly crushed in the accident. Both rear wheels also came off. Villagers, with the help of the police, pulled out the injured After seeing the accident, villagers called others and informed the police. The police reached the scene and, with the help of local residents, rescued the people trapped in the vehicle. The injured were then sent to the district hospital by ambulance. Mother and son die despite airbags deploying According to eyewitnesses, the Scorpio's airbags deployed during the collision, but the crash was so severe that Kshama and Anmol could not be saved. Three other people were seriously injured. After the accident, Greenfield Toll Plaza employees used a Hydra crane to pull the damaged Scorpio out of the ravine. The vehicle was then taken to Jangipur police station. ASP Dr Rakesh Kumar Mishra said: There were five people in the vehicle. All of them were travelling from Ballia to Varanasi. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examinations. The injured are undergoing treatment in Banaras. The case is being investigated."

stories.title: 'Hold elections using ballots and you will lose entire country':Congress fires back at PM Modi after BJP loses both MLC seats in Kashi to SP
stories.summary: The results for 11 MLC seats in Uttar Pradesh are out. The BJP has won four teacher and two graduate seats, taking its total to six. The Samajwadi Party (SP) has won two teacher and three graduate seats, taking its tally to five. The SP has gained two seats. Previously, the BJP held six of the 11 seats, the SP had three, the Teachers’ Association had one and an Independent candidate held one. This time, the Teachers’ Association has failed to win a single seat. After the results, Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate took a dig at the BJP. She said, “Modi ji, for now, you have lost all your strongholds. Hold elections using ballot papers, and you will lose the entire country.” Congress MP Pramod Tiwari said God had punished the BJP for stealing offerings. Meanwhile, posters were put up outside the SP headquarters in Lucknow following the BJP’s defeat in Kashi. They read, “Awadhesh Pasi won Ayodhya; Ashutosh and Lal Bihari won Kashi.” In Kashi, the BJP has once again lost both the teacher and graduate constituency seats. Counting for the graduate seat continued for more than 50 hours. The uproar that began at the counting centre late on Wednesday evening continued throughout the night. BJP candidate Kedarnath Singh also staged a sit-in protest. However, he accepted defeat on Thursday morning. Voting for five graduate and six teacher MLC seats in the state took place on 23 October. A total of 152 candidates were in the fray. Counting began at 8 am on 27 October. Around 1.481 million voters were eligible to vote across the two categories, of whom 818,000, or 55%, cast their votes. Go through our LIVE Blog for latest update…

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab brings rain to 20 UP districts:Police announce warning people not to step outside; weather to remain disturbed for 3 days
stories.summary: The impact of Cyclone 'Arnab', which formed over the Bay of Bengal, has begun to be felt in Uttar Pradesh. Today, Thursday, 21 districts have been warned of heavy rain, while 38 districts have been warned of storms and lightning. The weather changed suddenly in Lucknow and adjoining districts on Wednesday afternoon. Clouds gathered over Lucknow, followed by rain. Light rain was also reported in Rae Bareli. Weather experts said temperatures could drop by 5 to 8 degrees Celsius because of the impact of Cyclone Arnab. Professor Javed N. Malik of the Department of Earth Sciences at IIT Kanpur told Dainik Bhaskar that rain and strong winds could affect Uttar Pradesh. In view of Arnab's impact, State Relief Commissioner Bhanu Chandra Goswami directed officials in all districts to remain on alert for 24 hours. IMD and Agriculture Department issue guidelines for farmers Here is how much damage Cyclone Arnab could cause in Uttar Pradesh Crops will suffer the most damage because of Cyclone Arnab. It is the final week of October. At this time, the paddy crop has ripened and is being harvested. Preparations are also under way to sow wheat, potatoes and mustard. In such circumstances, unseasonal rain and strong winds could undo farmers' hard work. Rice to suffer the most damage: Prof. Ravi Shankar Singh, nodal officer at BHU's Rural Agriculture Meteorological Service Centre, and technical officer and meteorologist Shiv Mangal Singh said that the rice crop is currently either fully ripe and ready for harvesting or has already been harvested and is lying in the fields. Strong winds (40-50 km/h) will flatten the rice plants in the fields. If the harvested rice is submerged in water, the grains will turn black and begin to rot. Vegetables and horticulture: Waterlogging in the nurseries and fields of green vegetables such as cabbage, tomatoes and chillies will cause the plants to rot. In addition, banana and papaya trees are at the greatest risk of breaking or being uprooted by the strong winds. Delay in sowing potatoes and mustard: Farmers who were due to sow wheat, mustard or early potatoes in the coming days will be unable to sow them for at least 10 to 15 days because of waterlogging in the fields. This could delay the entire rabi season.
